items.body:
Bridal retailer wed2b is continuing its investment in large-format physical retail with the opening of its second London Megastore on Friday 6th November, following record-breaking initial sales at its Royal Victoria Dock flagship.
The new Holborn Megastore, located at 1 Thavies Inn, Holborn Circus, offers more than 10,000 sq ft of retail space and over 1,500 wedding dresses, available to browse, try on and take home the same day. Together with Royal Victoria Dock, which opened on 18 September, wed2b’s two London Megastores will offer more than 20,000 sq ft of retail space and over 3,000 wedding dresses across the capital.
The expansion follows a remarkable opening period at Royal Victoria Dock, providing encouraging early evidence of customer demand for wed2b’s investment in larger, technology-enabled bridal shopping environments. During its first six complete trading weeks, Royal Victoria Dock generated 6.6 times the average sales of stores across the rest of wed2b’s European network, while attracting 7.2 times the average store footfall.
The new flagship also significantly outperformed the retailer’s highest-performing established stores. Over the same six-week period, Royal Victoria Dock generated 144% more sales than Milton Keynes, the next highest-performing store in the network. Compared with wed2b’s former Baker Street location, Royal Victoria Dock achieved 232% higher sales during its first 44 days of trading than Baker Street recorded during the equivalent period in 2025.
The flagship’s opening period has established new company records for single-day and weekly sales, an encouraging result during a traditionally quieter period for bridal retail.
While these early results reflect a substantially larger store format and the activity surrounding its launch, they demonstrate strong initial customer interest in wed2b’s evolving retail proposition.
The opening of Holborn marks the next stage in wed2b’s development of its Megastore concept, which combines the retailer’s established no-appointment, take-home-today model with greater choice, dedicated customer spaces and technology designed to enhance the bridal shopping experience. The investment comes at a time when retailers across the UK are under increasing pressure to demonstrate the commercial value of their physical stores.
For wed2b, the strategy is about building on the strengths of its existing European network while exploring how larger, technology-enabled environments can create new opportunities for growth.
Todd Cassidy, Co-Founder and Managing Director of wed2b, said: “When we opened Royal Victoria Dock in September, we believed there was an exciting opportunity to take our retail model to another level. The response has been exceptional, with the store setting new company sales records during its opening weeks. But this isn’t simply about opening bigger shops. We’ve built wed2b around making wedding dress shopping easier, more transparent and more enjoyable, without losing any of the emotion that makes finding your dress so special. Our Megastores build on that same model, combining greater choice and immediate availability with personal service and technology that helps brides explore different styles and find what suits them Holborn represents another significant investment in physical retail, and we’re excited to continue developing the concept alongside our established stores across Europe.”
The Holborn Megastore combines the expertise of wed2b’s Bridal Experts with new digital experiences designed to make discovering the perfect dress more intuitive, engaging and enjoyable. Central to this is the installation of two AI-powered virtual try-on screens, replicating the technology introduced at Royal Victoria Dock in September. The screens have proved exceptionally popular at the first Megastore, where they are in near-constant use by brides exploring different styles and silhouettes. More than simply an entertaining experience, the technology provides a practical way for brides to preview wedding dresses from the store’s live stock selection, experiment with silhouettes they might not otherwise have considered and identify styles they would like to try on. The popularity of the experience at Royal Victoria Dock has reinforced wed2b’s belief that digital innovation can complement, rather than replace, the traditional fitting-room experience.
Brides visiting Holborn will be able to use the same technology alongside expert advice from wed2b’s Bridal Experts, before trying on their preferred dresses in person.
The store offers more than 1,500 gowns in sizes UK 6–30, with wedding dresses priced from £599 to £1,199. No appointment is required, and brides can take their chosen dress home on the day.
The importance of the physical shopping experience is also reflected in wed2b’s 2026 Bridal Report, which surveyed 11,437 brides across five European countries. The research found that 53% of brides purchased their wedding dress after visiting just one bridal boutique, highlighting the importance of the in-store experience in helping brides make confident purchasing decisions. The Megastore concept seeks to combine this personal connection with greater choice and technology that supports, rather than replaces, expert bridal advice.
The latest opening follows wed2b’s recent recognition at the Retail Week Awards 2027, where its Royal Victoria Dock Megastore has been shortlisted as a finalist in the Best New Large Store of the Year category. The award recognises innovation and excellence in physical retail, providing further recognition of wed2b’s investment in developing its next generation of stores.

Demand for behavioural support is growing, with Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line having helped more […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
The Pets Foundation, Pets at Home’s corporate foundation, is committing £1.2 million over three years to help fund Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line, giving more dog owners access to free, expert advice when they are struggling with their dog’s behaviour.
Demand for behavioural support is growing, with Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line having helped more than 35,000 dog owners since launching as a pilot in 2022. In the last year alone, 19,000 owners were supported, with over 40,000 calls completed. The team forecasts demand will continue to grow, with more than 20,000 dogs expected to be supported this year.
The £1.2 million investment reflects The Pets Foundation’s commitment to tackling the underlying causes that can lead to pets being given up. With behaviour-related issues accounting for over a third of dogs handed over to Dogs Trust, the funding will focus on early intervention, helping owners access trusted support before challenges escalate to the point where they feel unable to cope. Pets at Home stores, petcare advisors, and Vets for Pets practices will also help signpost owners to the Behaviour Support Line, making support easier to find.
The investment marks the next chapter in a 14-year relationship between Pets at Home and Dogs Trust, which has generated more than £6 million in value for the charity and supported over 100,000 dogs and their owners. Over the years, Pets at Home Group has supported Dogs Trust in a variety of ways, from providing food and essentials for dogs in its care to supporting veterinary care and local rehoming centres. The new funding builds on this relationship with a shared focus on helping more dogs stay in loving homes.
Behavioural challenges can place significant pressure on owners and their relationships with their dogs, making access to early, trusted support an important part of helping prevent problems from escalating.
Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line provides free, expert advice to all dog owners, offering a supportive and non-judgemental place to turn when they need help. As demand has increased, the service has expanded its opening hours and grown from a pilot team of three to a specialist team of over 20, with nearly two thirds of all callers getting the support they need over the phone.
Amy Angus, Head of Charity Partnership and Communities at Pets at Home, said:
“We know just how much pets mean to the people who love them, but behavioural challenges can sometimes leave owners feeling overwhelmed.
“The Behaviour Support Line gives owners somewhere to turn when they’re struggling, before those challenges reach a point of crisis. We want people to know that asking for help is okay, that they won’t be judged, and that giving up a much-loved pet isn’t their only option.
“That’s why we’re investing significantly in the helpline. By making trusted, expert advice easier for owners to access, we hope to tackle one of the key reasons dogs are given up and help more pets stay where they belong, in loving homes.”
Maria Murray, Dogs Trust Behaviour and Community Services Director said:
“We’re incredibly grateful to The Pets Foundation for this significant investment and proud to be continuing a relationship with Pets at Home that has lasted more than a decade. What has always united us is a shared ambition to make life better for dogs and the people who love them.
“The real value of this funding will be felt long beyond an individual phone call. Giving an owner the right advice at the right time can change the course of a dog’s life, building understanding and confidence and, in some cases, helping a family stay together. With The Pets Foundation’s support, we’ll be able to make that difference for many more dogs and their owners.”
The Behaviour Support Line in action – Barney’s Story
The difference the right behavioural support can make can be seen in Barney’s story. Barney settled in well after moving into foster care, but his carers became concerned that he was resource guarding. This is a behaviour where a dog becomes protective of something they consider valuable, such as food, toys or other possessions. Barney could become protective around his food bowl, a favourite toy or even a shoe, particularly when the other dog in the home came close.
His foster carers managed the situation by feeding the dogs separately, toys were supervised, and situations that might cause conflict were avoided, but another incident occurred and they contacted Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line for additional support.
After talking through Barney’s routine and behaviour, the team helped his carers understand the anxiety behind his resource guarding and suggested some simple changes. These included feeding Barney before his morning walk to reduce the anticipation around mealtimes, preventing him from entering the kitchen while food was being prepared, and giving him plenty of uninterrupted space while eating. They were also given practical guidance on managing resource guarding and relationships within a multi-dog household.
“Once we understood why Barney was behaving the way he was, it all started to make much more sense. We had a plan to follow and felt much more confident moving forward,” said his foster carer, James.
With the new routine and management in place, there were no further incidents, and Barney became calmer and more settled.
“The difference was huge,” said James, “We could all relax a bit more, and Barney seemed much happier too.”
After six weeks in foster care, he found a loving new home and was adopted in July 2026, where he has continued to thrive.
His story shows how understanding the reasons behind a dog’s behaviour, and getting support when you need it, can make all the difference. With a little patience, the right advice and plenty of love, Barney was able to put his best paw forward and start the next chapter of his life.

items.body:
Herne Bay Co-op re-opens its doors and welcomes the community back in-store following a near four-week investment programme to enhance the store.
The store – located in Reculver Road in the Herne Bay community of Beltinge – opens between 7am-10pm daily and conveniently offers Co-op’s extensive range and choice of fresh and healthy products, meal ideas, food to go, Fairtrade products; an extended in-store bakery, and award-winning chilled beers and wines.
There is also a focus on seasonal food and drink, including Co-op’s Christmas sandwich range packed with festive flavours.
The online home delivery of groceries is available through Just Eat, Uber Eats and Deliveroo – with orders picked fresh in the store and delivered quickly and conveniently in the community.
New refrigeration has been installed throughout which is not only more energy efficient and supports Co-op’s carbon reduction journey, but also extends the range and choice of fresh and frozen goods.
Added services include Lottery; payment services via PayPoint and an ATM providing access to cash in the community.
Soft plastic recycling is also available so shoppers can return and recycle materials that are often not universally accepted via household kerbside recycling, such as crisp packets and bread bags, lids from ready meals, biscuit wrappers and, pet food pouches.
Karen Butler, Co-op’s store manager, said: “We are delighted to re-open, and the whole team is really enjoying welcoming our members and customers back into the store – we have had a great response. We work to ensure the store is a hub contributing to local life and meeting the needs of our community. With a focus on offering quality products, value and choice that can be enjoyed by everyone, we have deals and promotions throughout the store, and a range of added services to make everyday life easier. We’re proud to have the opportunity to serve Herne Bay, the team is here to contribute to local life and conveniently serve and support the community.”
Committed to backing British agriculture, all of Co-op’s own meat, poultry and dairy is 100% British – including in its pies, ready meals and sandwiches.
Fairtrade products are available across the store supporting farmers, workers and their communities around the world who grow and produce products and ingredients for Co-op.
With its history dating back more than 180 years, Co-op is one of the world’s largest consumer-owned co-operatives. Co-op exists to create value for its membership and communities, its more than 7.6 million members own the business and play an intrinsic part in the governance of the organisation.
More information about the benefits of Co-op Membership is available by visiting coop.co.uk/membership

The launch comes as Britain’s love of café-quality coffee at home continues to grow, with […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Cafédirect is expanding its whole bean organic coffee range with the launch of its award-winning Mayan Gold in a new 750g format, available in Tesco from 9 November 2026, as well as through the Cafédirect website and selected online retailers.
The launch comes as Britain’s love of café-quality coffee at home continues to grow, with UK bean-to-cup coffee machine sales reportedly rising by 33.5% and whole bean coffee sales increasing by 20.3% in volume over the past year¹.
And with Christmas approaching, coffee-making equipment is firmly on shoppers’ wish lists. New research from Lakeland reveals that 28% of Brits would welcome a coffee machine or coffee-making accessories as a Christmas gift², making Mayan Gold 750g a timely addition for coffee lovers looking to get the most from their home brewing experience.
Designed for engaged whole bean drinkers using bean-to-cup machines or grinding their own beans, the new 750g pack offers a convenient, better-value way to enjoy great coffee at home. Building on the success of Cafédirect’s existing Machu Picchu 750g format, the launch provides a natural trade-up opportunity for loyal Mayan Gold 200g shoppers, while giving Machu Picchu fans an exciting new single origin flavour to explore.
Sourced from the highlands of Mexico, including Chiapas, Mayan Gold is a single origin Arabica coffee that captures the rich character of its origins.
Grown among misty cloud forests and lush tropical jungle, where shade and mist help coffee cherries ripen slowly, Mayan Gold is celebrated for its smooth, rounded character and natural sweetness.
Warm, smooth and naturally sweet, the coffee offers soft caramel notes that develop into rich brown sugar and light molasses. Its dark roast delivers a velvety body, gentle acidity and a beautifully balanced, warm and lingering finish.
Versatile enough to suit a variety of brewing methods, Mayan Gold is ideal for bean-to-cup and espresso machines, as well as moka pots, AeroPress, pour-over, filter coffee and cafetières. Whether coffee lovers prefer a rich morning espresso or a leisurely cafetière, Mayan Gold makes it easy to enjoy great-tasting coffee at home.
For shoppers who care about more than just what’s in their cup, Cafédirect combines exceptional coffee with a commitment to putting growers first.
Founded in 1991, Cafédirect has spent more than 30 years championing a fairer way of doing business and building long-term relationships with coffee-growing communities.
As a pioneer of Fairtrade coffee in the UK, a social enterprise and a certified B Corp, Cafédirect is committed to making great coffee that benefits the people who grow it. Mayan Gold is both Organic and Fairtrade certified, offering consumers the reassurance that their everyday coffee choice supports more responsible farming and fairer trading practices.
And Cafédirect’s commitment goes beyond certification. The brand works closely with farmer cooperatives, giving growers a voice in the business and investing in initiatives designed to improve livelihoods and support more resilient coffee-growing communities.
Central to this approach is Cafédirect’s living income commitment, making it the first UK company to commit to paying Living Income Reference Prices by 2030, helping coffee farmers earn enough to support their families, invest in their farms and build a more secure future.
For coffee lovers seeking great taste, better value and a brand that shares their values, Mayan Gold 750g brings all three together.
Paige Langran, senior brand manager, Cafédirect, comments: “There’s something special about making a really great cup of coffee at home, and we’re seeing more people embrace that experience. Whether they’ve invested in a bean-to-cup machine or love grinding their own beans, coffee drinkers are becoming more adventurous about the flavours and origins they choose.
“Following the success of our Machu Picchu 750g coffee, we’re delighted to introduce Mayan Gold in the same larger format. With its beautifully smooth character, natural caramel sweetness and rich brown sugar notes, it’s a fantastic choice for coffee lovers looking to explore new flavours, while giving existing Mayan Gold fans more of the coffee they love. Sales are up over 20% year on year on our 750g packs, showing our customers not only want ethical coffee, but to stock up on more of their favourite coffee.
“And for us, great coffee isn’t just about how it tastes. From our Fairtrade and Organic credentials to our commitment to supporting living incomes for coffee farmers, we’re working to make coffee better for the people who grow it, too.
“We believe you shouldn’t have to choose between great taste and doing the right thing. With Cafédirect, you can have both of these. That’s what we mean by coffee done right.”
Cafédirect Mayan Gold 750g Whole Bean Coffee launches on 9 November 2026 in Tesco, on the Cafédirect website and through selected online retailers. RRP £17.25.

Starbucks is set to welcome 7,500 new baristas across the UK over the next five years, alongside its plan to open 500 new coffeehouses across the country. The expansion will create thousands of opportunities for people to build their careers, with new baristas joining more than 18,000 employees already bringing the Starbucks Experience to life […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Starbucks is set to welcome 7,500 new baristas across the UK over the next five years, alongside its plan to open 500 new coffeehouses across the country.
The expansion will create thousands of opportunities for people to build their careers, with new baristas joining more than 18,000 employees already bringing the Starbucks Experience to life for customers every day.
People in the Midlands, North of England, Wales and Scotland will see the most Starbucks jobs coming to their communities, with approximately 80 per cent of new coffeehouses targeted in areas north of the M25.
Darren King, vice president and managing director, Starbucks UK, said: ‘We’re proud to be creating thousands of new jobs across the UK over the next five years, bringing new opportunities to communities across the country as we continue to invest and grow here.
At the heart of our Back to Starbucks strategy is our ambition to create a place where people can build skills, grow their careers and feel part of a team. We’re deeply focused on how we can help more young people into these positions, starting by making entry level roles as accessible as possible. You don’t need previous industry experience and we’ll give you the training and support you need from day one’.
Starbucks is a major employer of young people in the UK with more than half (53 per cent) of partners in Starbucks company-operated stores under the age of 24.
Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the BRC, said: “At a time when too many young people are struggling to get a foot on the career ladder, this investment is hugely welcome. Retail and hospitality are vital routes into the workplace, helping young people build skills, confidence and experience while offering genuine opportunities to progress. Starbucks commitment to thousands of new jobs shows the important role the industry can play in opening doors for the next generation.”
To better understand young people’s perceptions of customer-facing roles in retail and hospitality, Starbucks commissioned research with Ipsos involving approximately 3,400 young people. The findings revealed that of the 18-35-year-olds surveyed who are currently, or have previously worked in a customer-facing job in the retail or hospitality industry (n=2392), 83% think the experience has helped them develop skills that will be useful in their working life including customer service skills, communication and teamwork.
Despite this, many young people do not see retail and hospitality as a long-term career path. Just 10% of those currently working in customer-facing roles in these sectors expect to remain in their role for more than 10 years. More generally, 68% of 18–35-year-olds surveyed agree that retail and hospitality roles are perceived as temporary or ‘stopgap’ work.
To help challenge this perception, Starbucks is creating more opportunities for baristas to grow their careers as the business grows, with clear pathways from a first job to a lasting career.
With more than 6,000 leaders already working in coffeehouses across the country, Starbucks is investing further in its leadership pipeline by creating an additional 140 deputy store manager roles. This builds on existing initiatives, including its Accelerated Leadership Programme, designed to give baristas an accelerated route into leadership and help them build the skills to become store manager-ready in approximately 13 months, compared with a journey that would typically take around three years.
Starbucks is also expanding the routes available for employees to learn, develop and build long-term careers with the business. It has committed to a further 200 apprenticeship places over the next year, building on the more than 2,000 employees who have already taken part in its fee-free apprenticeship programme. Opportunities span from Level 2 entry-level barista apprenticeships through to advanced professional qualifications for senior leaders, giving employees the chance to continue developing at every stage of their career.
The findings also come as routes into work are changing for young people. The research found that 68%* of those surveyed agree that AI is reducing traditional entry-level jobs available to young people aged 18-25. At the same time, almost one million 16–24-year-olds in the UK are currently not in education, employment or training.
King added: “These findings show that we need to rethink how we value hospitality careers. Working face-to-face with customers, colleagues and managers helps build vital interpersonal skills that can provide the foundation for any career, with 83% of young people with experience in these roles recognising the valuable skills they gain. But beyond developing transferable skills, we want more young people to see the opportunities to build a rewarding career in hospitality.
“That’s why we’re creating more ways for people to grow and progress at Starbucks. For those with a passion for coffee, programmes like Coffee Masters recognise our most skilled baristas and offer advanced coffee education. And for those who want to explore a different path, there are opportunities across our wider business, from beverage development to finance, marketing and much more.”

items.title: ShopKind Week and National Week of Action puts retail crime and abuse in the spotlight
items.summary: A joint national week of action to tackle retail abuse and crime, backed by policing minister Sarah Jones, is bringing together the retail sector, policing and partners and uniting four national campaigns for the first time from today, Monday 9 November. The Association of Convenience… This story continues at ShopKind Week and National Week of Action puts retail crime and abuse in the spotlight Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The Association of Convenience Stores (ACS), Usdaw, the Retail Trust and the National Business Crime Centre (NBCC) are joining forces for a coordinated response to the scale of the issue, combining activity in shops and workplaces with public campaigning.
Running from 9 -15 November 2026, the partnership will unite ACS’s ShopKind, Usdaw’s Respect for Shopworkers Week, the Retail Trust’s Let’s Respect Retail and NBCC’s Safer Business Action Week.
Together, they will encourage respect for retail workers, call on shoppers to change their behaviour and support practical action against crime affecting businesses and their communities.
Preparations span workplace events, public advertising and support for retailers to take part in stores, alongside a coordinated policing response.
Partner activity planned for the week includes:
- ACS – ShopKind: With 173 supporting organisations, ShopKind will be promoted through national and trade media, with updated materials for stores and social media. Supporters are being encouraged to publicly endorse the campaign and nominate ShopKind Champions to share its messages.
- Usdaw – Respect for Shopworkers Week: Representative-led campaigning is planned in around 1,000 retail workplaces, backed by major retailers. Messages will ask shoppers to “Keep Your Cool” and workers to “Report It – Sort It”. Usdaw will also release interim findings from its 2026 Freedom From Fear survey of retail workers’ experiences.
- Retail Trust – Let’s Respect Retail: A new report by the charity will show the scale of shop staff abuse and its impact on workers, alongside calls for shoppers to treat shop workers respectfully appearing in thousands of stores, shop windows, shopping centres, cinemas and transport hubs. Employees at some of the country’s biggest retailers and shopping centres are also being given more support by the Retail Trust to help them respond to and deal with abusive incidents.
- NBCC – Safer Business Action Week: The NBCC is coordinating the policing response, with 20 forces already confirming participation. Forces are encouraged to work with businesses, Business Crime Reduction Partnerships and Business Improvement Districts on local activity covering prevention, intelligence, enforcement and engagement. This could include targeting prolific offenders, sharing intelligence on crime hotspots and improving incident reporting.
Crime and policing minister Sarah Jones said: “Retail workers are the backbone of our high streets, and no one should face abuse, threats or violence simply for doing their job.
“I am proud to support this national week of action, which brings together retailers, police and local partners to tackle the abuse, theft and antisocial behaviour that affects communities across the country.
“Shop theft is finally falling and there are thousands more neighbourhood police on our streets. But we won’t stop there. We are clear that retail crime is not minor and those responsible will be held accountable.”
Superintendent Lisa Maslen, National Business Crime Centre lead, said: “The strength of this week is the partnership behind it. Bringing all four campaigns together for the first time means we can reach more businesses, hear directly from shopworkers and turn that shared commitment into local action.
“With 20 police forces already signed up, preparations are gathering pace. Alongside our partners’ work in stores and communities, policing will focus on preventing crime, sharing intelligence and targeting the offenders causing the greatest harm.”
Association of Convenience Stores chief executive Ed Woodall said: “We are delighted at the support for the ShopKind campaign shown in thousands of shops across the UK and believe that bringing ShopKind Week together with leading awareness campaigns from shopworkers union USDAW, the Retail Trust and the National Business Crime Centre, sends a clear united message that colleagues shouldn’t have to face abuse, that the businesses they work for will report incidents, and that the police will respond effectively.
“Together with the backing of tougher legislation, we can make a real positive difference to hundreds of thousands of people working in our nation’s local shops.”
The four partners have been encouraging businesses to use campaign materials, involve staff and link up with their local police and business partnerships to plan activity during the week.

items.body:
Virgin Atlantic Holidays has expanded its partnership with M&S with plans to open a concession at the retailer’s Westfield White City store.
Due to open in December 2026, the concession will offer shoppers personalised advice and booking services for long-haul holidays, including family trips, multi-centre breaks and luxury escapes.
The latest announcement forms part of the travel company’s wider investment in London, following its recently announced flagship at Battersea Power Station.
It also builds on the loyalty partnership launched earlier this year between M&S Sparks and Virgin Red, which gives members more ways to earn and spend rewards across the two programmes.
The concession will extend that relationship into in-store holiday planning as Virgin Atlantic Holidays looks to reach more of the capital’s premium leisure travellers.
Virgin Atlantic chief commercial officer Dave Geer said: “M&S is a brand people know and love, and this new concession gives customers another convenient way to start thinking about, planning and booking their next holiday.”
He added: “Together with our new flagship store at Battersea Power Station, this opening is an important part of our investment in London and our ambition to make Virgin Atlantic Holidays more visible and accessible across the capital.”

items.title: Peak season 2026: What’s changed, and how do you win?
items.summary: Retailers are, of course, now entering into another golden quarter. However, this year looks slightly different. Whilst the core challenge of the season remains, supply chain disruption, changing shopper habits and a good portion of uncertainty mean that many leaders are struggling to see what peak this year is going to look like. To get...
items.body:
Retailers are, of course, now entering into another golden quarter. However, this year looks slightly different. Whilst the core challenge of the season remains, supply chain disruption, changing shopper habits and a good portion of uncertainty mean that many leaders are struggling to see what peak this year is going to look like.
To get to the heart of peak preparedness, Retail Gazette’s Unpacked podcast catches up with Charlotte Jamieson, VP advertiser and agency partnerships at Cardlytics to delve into the company’s recent research, and find out why some unexpected strategic tweaks could ensure that 2026’s golden quarter is a success.
“The whole landscape of retail has changed, and the golden quarter will be no exception to that,” says Jamieson. “What the data shows us is that shoppers are managing their budgets hard, even at Christmas. They’re shopping around, they’re trading down, they’re breaking old brand loyalties. We do see that they’re still spending, but only when something prompts them.”
“For retailers, it’s not whether the demand exists, but if you’re shopping up for shoppers at the right time, with the right relevance, and with the right value,” Jamieson adds.
Listen now to find out more, and check out the Retail Gazette Golden Guide ’26 for more insight into how to win this season.

items.title: Greggs and Too Good To Go save over 7m bags of surplus food
items.summary: Greggs and Too Good To Go have reportedly saved more than seven million bags of surplus food from going to waste since launching their partnership in 2021. The bakery chain…
items.body:
Greggs and Too Good To Go save over 7m bags of surplus food
Greggs and Too Good To Go have reportedly saved more than seven million bags of surplus food from going to waste since launching their partnership in 2021.
The bakery chain has worked with the food waste reduction platform for five years, offering customers discounted surplus products through its app.
The partnership allows shoppers to purchase Surprise Bags containing unsold food from Greggs stores at the end of the day and in the early morning, alongside Grab Bags featuring surplus hot food at various points throughout the day.
Greggs Grab Bags are now available in more than 2,000 shops across the UK, with prices starting at £2.99.
Customers can reserve and pay for the bags through the free Too Good To Go app before collecting them from their chosen store, with contents depending on what is available.
Too Good To Go UK and Ireland managing director Chelsea Kerr said: “Autumn is a great reminder of why partnerships like ours with Greggs matter. Routines get busier, budgets get tighter, and people want food that’s convenient and good value.
“Greggs has been partnered with us for five years, and together we’ve shown how a much-loved high street brand can make preventing food waste part of everyday life.”
The initiative forms part of Greggs’ efforts to reduce food waste across its store estate while offering customers lower-cost food options.
Greggs retail operations director Gillian Long said: “Our partnership with Too Good To Go plays an important role in redistributing unsold food.
“Whether it’s a bake, sandwich or sweet treat that’s being saved, it gives our customers a simple way to pick up something they love while helping us make sure good food doesn’t go to waste.”

items.summary: Marks & Spencer has appointed former Waitrose executive Alan Hoe as its new head of customer experience and operations, bringing more than two decades of grocery retail experience to the…
items.body:
M&S appoints former Waitrose executive Alan Hoe as customer experience boss
Marks & Spencer has appointed former Waitrose executive Alan Hoe as its new head of customer experience and operations, bringing more than two decades of grocery retail experience to the business.
Hoe joins the retailer after spending 21 years at Waitrose, where he held several positions, including retail proposition lead for front end and services.
Most recently, he worked as a consultant at customer experience consultancy CLX, advising on customer experience.
His appointment comes as M&S continues to invest in improving its stores, customer experience and operational efficiency as part of its wider transformation strategy.
The retailer recently reported a strong performance across its food business, with sales rising 13.9 per cent to £5.16bn in the 26 weeks to 26 September.
Like-for-like food sales increased 11.7 per cent, while adjusted operating profit climbed to £288.6m as the supermarket continued to attract shoppers through investment in value, quality and innovation.
M&S has also been accelerating investment in its store estate, completing 18 new, extended or renewed stores during the first half as it looks to improve the shopping experience and drive further growth.

items.title: Morrisons unveils Goldilocks-inspired Christmas advert starring the Three Bears
items.summary: Morrisons has unveiled its 2026 Christmas advert, putting a modern twist on Goldilocks and the Three Bears to celebrate the personal touches that make the festive season special. The supermarket’s…
items.body:
Morrisons unveils Goldilocks-inspired Christmas advert starring the Three Bears
Morrisons has unveiled its 2026 Christmas advert, putting a modern twist on Goldilocks and the Three Bears to celebrate the personal touches that make the festive season special.
The supermarket’s 90-second campaign, titled ‘Christmas Made Just Right’, will debut on ITV, Channel 4, Five and Sky TV today at 9.15pm.
The advert follows Mummy and Daddy Bear as they prepare to welcome their grown-up son and his new girlfriend home for Christmas.
Daddy Bear visits Morrisons Market Street, where the supermarket’s skilled bakers, butchers, fishmongers and deli colleagues help him prepare the family’s festive feast, including an enormous salmon.
Meanwhile, Mummy Bear attempts to get the family home ready, with a few mishaps along the way.
When Baby Bear finally arrives, his girlfriend is revealed to be Goldilocks, who discovers a warm and welcoming Christmas celebration complete with a wonky tree, mismatched decorations and a carefully prepared festive spread.
The campaign aims to showcase Morrisons’ ‘fresh food expertise and its ability to cater to different tastes and family traditions’.
Morrisons marketing and advertising director Beverley Lumb said: “Everyone has their own idea of what makes Christmas ‘just right’ alongside their own family traditions that make the day feel truly magical.
“As Christmas comes in all shapes and sizes, we pride ourselves on delivering good, honest value, ensuring every piece of festive fare is crafted with the thought, care and quality for everyone gathered around your table.”
The advert was created by Leo UK and directed by Nick Ball, whose previous work includes campaigns for Tesco, Ikea and Uber Eats.
The Three Bears are brought to life using animatronics, with each character given their own distinct personality.
Alongside the TV campaign, Morrisons is launching a series of social media activations, including a Baby Bear takeover, teaser content across Instagram and TikTok, and a special Gogglebox partnership featuring the show’s stars reacting to the advert.
The supermarket is also releasing an exclusive cuddly bear toy, with 50p from every sale donated to Marie Curie.
Leo UK chief creative officer Andrew Long said: “Goldilocks and the Three Bears is a story generations know, but people experience stories very differently today.
“So we’ve built the campaign to work in different ways too: our Christmas TV spot tells the parents’ story, while our social takeover gives Baby Bear his own voice.”

items.title: More than half of shop workers face weekly abuse as attacks surge ahead of Christmas
items.summary: More than half of UK shop workers are now facing abuse every week, with rising violence, intimidation and unwanted filming prompting calls for shoppers to show greater respect ahead of the Christmas trading period. New research from the Retail Trust found that 54 per cent of retail workers experience abuse weekly, up from 43 per...
items.body:
More than half of UK shop workers are now facing abuse every week, with rising violence, intimidation and unwanted filming prompting calls for shoppers to show greater respect ahead of the Christmas trading period.
New research from the Retail Trust found that 54 per cent of retail workers experience abuse weekly, up from 43 per cent last year and 33 per cent in 2024.
The charity’s annual survey of 1,138 shop workers revealed that 79 per cent had experienced abuse or violence from members of the public over the past year, compared with 77 per cent in 2025.
Almost a quarter reported experiencing abuse involving a physical attack, while 38 per cent said they or a colleague had been filmed without consent, up from 30 per cent last year.
The findings highlight the growing impact of retail crime and aggressive customer behaviour on staff wellbeing, with 70 per cent of those affected by abuse reporting stress or anxiety about going to work.
More than a third said they felt unsafe at work, while 48 per cent admitted that worsening abuse had made them consider quitting their job or leaving retail altogether, up from 43 per cent in 2025.
Meanwhile, 84 per cent had witnessed shoplifting over the past year, with 35 per cent witnessing it daily.
The Retail Trust is launching its nationwide ‘Let’s Respect Retail‘ campaign today, urging shoppers to show greater kindness towards store workers during the busy festive period.
The initiative, backed by retailers including Sainsbury’s, Next, Currys, EE and Holland & Barrett, will see messages encouraging customers to ‘start with hello’ displayed across thousands of stores, shopping centres, cinemas and railway stations.
Retail Trust chief executive Chris Brook-Carter said: “Our country’s shop workers have had enough of being shouted at, threatened, and treated with contempt.
“We’re hearing from people who are frightened to come into work because they don’t know what they’ll face that day, and from others who have been pushed to breaking point by repeated abuse.”
He added that aggressive customer behaviour was increasingly being viewed as part of the job, damaging staff morale and driving experienced workers out of the sector.
British Retail Consortium chief executive Helen Dickinson said: “No one should go to work fearing for their safety, yet the Retail Trust’s findings are a stark reminder that violence and abuse against retail workers remain endemic.”
Sainsbury’s chief retail, logistics and supply chain officer Tracey Clements said the supermarket was investing heavily in measures to identify offenders, prevent them from returning to stores and work with police to hold them accountable.
“No retailer can tackle this alone and we’re standing with the Retail Trust to ask everyone to treat the colleagues helping them with the kindness and respect they deserve,” she said.
The campaign also has the backing of retail entrepreneur Theo Paphitis, who said kindness was essential to creating a positive working environment for store teams.
Despite the findings, the Retail Trust’s research revealed that 83% of employees said just one positive customer interaction during their shift could help them recover from a negative experience.
The campaign is being delivered alongside the Association of Convenience Stores, shopworkers’ union Usdaw and the National Business Crime Centre as part of a dedicated week of action tackling violence and abuse against retail workers.

Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Morrisons Christmas advert will make its national TV debut on Monday 9th November at 9.15pm on multiple major networks including ITV, Channel 4, Five and Sky TV with a modern retelling of the Goldilocks story in which everyone likes things a little differently. For the early birds, highlight clips will also be dropping across Instagram and TikTok from 6:00am.
The new 90-second ad brings Goldilocks and the Three Bears together for Christmas, playing on the familiar idea that everyone likes things a little differently. At its heart are Morrisons skilled bakers, butchers, fishmongers and deli colleagues, who make and prepare food in store and help customers find the right cuts, portions and food for their own Christmas tables.
The advert tells the familiar story of a Mum and Dad preparing for their grown-up child to bring a partner home for Christmas for the first time. It just so happens that these parents are Mummy & Daddy Bear.
Daddy Bear heads to Morrisons Market Street, where its skilled fresh food makers help him prepare the family’s festive spread including an enormous salmon, with expert cooking instructions provided by a Morrisons Fishmonger to ensure it’s ‘just right’ for the big day. At home Mummy Bear sets about making the house just right, with a few bear-shaped mishaps along the way. When Baby Bear finally arrives, his new girlfriend is revealed as Goldilocks.
As ‘Goldie’ steps inside, she finds a Christmas that is warm and welcoming rather than fairy-tale flawless. The tree is wonky, the decorations and place settings do not match and her chair is showing signs of disrepair. Her face lights up at the beautiful, homely Christmas and mouthwatering spread with a perfectly sized place setting for each of them. As she sits down to dinner, it is clear that everything has been chosen and prepared with love and care, especially for her.
The advert ends with the campaign line: “Christmas Made Just Right”.
Beverley Lumb, Marketing and Advertising Director at Morrisons, said: “Everyone has their own idea of what makes Christmas ‘just right’ alongside their own family traditions that make the day feel truly magical. As Christmas comes in all shapes and sizes, we pride ourselves on delivering good, honest value, ensuring every piece of festive fare is crafted with the thought, care and quality for everyone gathered around your table.”
“From award-winning smoked salmon and perfectly sliced glazed Christmas ham, to golden mince pies, freshly baked in store or British-grown fresh veg, our skilled bakers, fishmongers, butchers, and deli teams craft fresh food daily and help customers find exactly what they need, from the right cut to the perfect portion.”
The ad was directed by award-winning film maker Nick Ball, whose credits include campaigns for Uber Eats, Tesco and IKEA and work with Mariah Carey, Chris Hemsworth, Tina Fey and Christopher Walken. The Three Bears are brought to life as animatronic characters, with each given their own personality and performance.
Andrew Long, Chief Creative Officer at Leo UK, said: “There’s a huge amount of craft in bringing a family everyone knows to life and giving each bear their own personality. For us at Leo, this is also a great example of Populist Creativity that gets people talking. Goldilocks and the Three Bears is a story generations know, but people experience stories very differently today. So we’ve built the campaign to work in different ways too: our Christmas TV spot tells the parents’ story, while our social takeover gives Baby Bear his own voice. Each generation gets its own way into the story, just as Morrisons helps people make Christmas ‘just right’ for all the different tastes around their table. ”
For little ones who are eager to bring the magic to life, Morrisons is launching an exclusive cuddly bear plush toy, with 50p from the sale of every bear being donated to Marie Curie.

items.title: Poundland blocked from buying new stock despite £86m turnaround
items.summary: Poundland has reportedly been blocked from ordering new stock ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period, despite an £86m improvement in its financial performance over the past year. The embattled company has been unable to pay suppliers for new products since 27 October after owner Gordon Brothers restricted its access to credit facilities and cash...
items.body:
Poundland has reportedly been blocked from ordering new stock ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period, despite an £86m improvement in its financial performance over the past year.
The embattled company has been unable to pay suppliers for new products since 27 October after owner Gordon Brothers restricted its access to credit facilities and cash generated through trading, according to ITV News.
The restrictions mean Poundland is continuing to sell its existing inventory, but cannot replenish its shelves, raising fresh concerns over its ability to continue trading.
As of 3 November, Poundland reportedly had around £25m in cash that management was unable to access, despite the balance continuing to grow through store sales.
Poundland boss Barry Williams revealed a dramatic improvement in the retailer’s financial performance in a message to staff on Friday.
According to the internal memo, seen by ITV News, Poundland swung from an EBITDA loss of £68.1m in the financial year to September 2025 to a profit of £18.1m in the year to September 2026.
The £86.2m turnaround comes as like-for-like sales continue to improve, with sales rising seven per cent in the first period of the new financial year.
Trading strengthened further during Halloween week, when like-for-like sales jumped 11.4 per cent year on year and exceeded budget by £1.5m.
Williams acknowledged that total sales remained below last year’s levels but attributed the decline to the closure of 115 stores as part of the retailer’s restructuring programme.
The figures have yet to be audited.
However, Gordon Brothers, which acquired Poundland from Pepco Group for £1 in June 2025, has maintained that the business remains financially vulnerable despite its improving performance.
In a letter to the government last week, Gordon Brothers’ UK operations boss Mark Newton-Jones warned that rising inflation, higher employment costs and shoplifting continued to put pressure on the company.
He said Poundland was still not generating cash at a sustainable level, despite its turnaround efforts.
Martin Property Group and Xyra Group Holdings are among the parties to have submitted proposals to acquire Poundland as a going concern.
Meanwhile, Tesco, B&M, Iceland, Poundstretcher, The Range and Lidl have all expressed interest in acquiring parts of the retailer’s store estate.
Martin Property Group has reportedly urged Gordon Brothers to release funding to allow Poundland to replenish stock and keep trading while rescue negotiations continue.
Poundland’s management has also held talks with the government, with Williams and chief financial officer Shaun Wills meeting business minister Kate Dearden last week.
Gordon Brothers is set to face scrutiny from MPs over its handling of the retailer’s financial difficulties, with the Business and Trade Committee due to hear evidence from company executives in private on Wednesday.
Poundland’s notice of intention to appoint administrators is due to expire on Thursday 12 November, leaving just days to secure a deal that could safeguard more than 10,000 jobs.

items.body:
Police have warned that shoppers hunting for cut-price deals on resale platforms such as Vinted, eBay and Facebook Marketplace are inadvertently fuelling organised shoplifting gangs.
Criminal networks are now regularly turning to online marketplaces to sell goods stolen from high street retailers. As such, shoppers have been urged to question heavily discounted products advertised as brand new.
National Business Crime Centre lead Superintendent Lisa Maslen told The Telegraph that organised gangs were ‘exploiting women and children’ to steal products from stores, before selling them through legitimate-looking online listings.
She warned that clothing advertised as ‘brand new with tags’ could be a particular red flag, especially when offered at prices significantly below their retail value.
“If it seems too good to be true and too good a price, then you know there’s something wrong. Trust your instincts,” Maslen said.
The police chief urged consumers to consider the wider consequences of buying potentially stolen goods, warning that demand was helping sustain criminal activity on Britain’s high streets.
Maslen is set to host a summit in January alongside Home Office officials and representatives from Vinted, Facebook Marketplace and Gumtree to tackle the growing use of online resale platforms by organised crime groups.
Research commissioned by the NBCC and backed by the Home Office, found that shoplifting remained profitable because criminals could quickly convert stolen stock into cash through online marketplaces, rogue businesses and other resale channels.
The report called for greater collaboration between police, retailers and online platforms to disrupt the networks handling stolen goods.
The British Independent Retailers Association has also urged marketplaces to take greater responsibility for preventing stolen products from being sold through their platforms.
Bira chief executive Andrew Goodacre previously warned that disrupting the markets making theft profitable was just as important as catching offenders.
Currently, more than 500,000 shoplifting offences are recorded annually across England and Wales.
Usdaw general secretary Joanne Thomas said shop theft had doubled since the pandemic, with offenders becoming increasingly brazen and organised.
Meanwhile, eBay insisted it prohibits the sale of stolen goods and uses technology to identify suspicious activity, alongside working with police to support investigations.

items.body:
Morrisons was named Overall Winner at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, which took place in Central London last week. And it also emerged victorious in the RTIH Editor's Choice category for its partnership with Gatekeeper Systems.
In a LinkedIn post, the UK grocery giant said: "We’re delighted to have been named Overall Winner, selected by the judging panel as the standout entry from across all of the event's 23 categories. Great recognition for some of the brilliant and innovative cross functional projects that have been delivered over the last few months!"
It added: "We were also recognised in the Editor’s Choice Award, alongside Gatekeeper Systems for our Cart Control programme across five Morrisons stores. The programme has delivered some fantastic results: An estimated 82.1 tonnes of CO₂e saved each year; 1,170 fewer replacement trolleys needed; 7,696 fewer trolleys ending up in local communities and waterways. Congratulations to everyone involved in making this possible!"
Scott Thompson, Editor and Founder at RTIH, said: "Congratulations to Morrisons. We received a record number of entries this year, showcasing truly impressive innovation across both traditional and digital retail spaces."
"To quote a member of our judging panel: Reviewing such inventive, high impact solutions has been a truly rewarding experience. The depth of engineering, scalable architecture, and strategic vision displayed throughout the submissions underscores the rapid transformation happening across modern retail technology."
"A number of companies were in the running for Overall Winner but ultimately the judges picked Morrisons for launching several innovative initiatives encompassing major technological upgrades to enhance its customers’ shopping experience."

items.title: Swedish grocery retailers come together on food climate data as FoodFacts footprints 120,000+ products
items.summary: FoodFacts reports that it now delivers comparable carbon footprints for more than 120,000 food products every week to retailers ICA Sweden, Coop Sweden and Axfood, which together represent around 90% of the Swedish grocery market. The initiative addresses two key challenges: agreeing how food emissi
items.body:
FoodFacts reports that it now delivers comparable carbon footprints for more than 120,000 food products every week to retailers ICA Sweden, Coop Sweden and Axfood, which together represent around 90% of the Swedish grocery market.
The initiative addresses two key challenges: agreeing how food emissions should be calculated and having the technology to apply those calculations consistently at scale.
To establish a common approach, the Swedish Food Retailers’ Federation and the Swedish Food Federation commissioned the Swedish research institute RISE to develop an industry methodology for calculating food related carbon footprints, first published in 2023. In 2025, FoodFacts was selected to operationalise the methodology across the grocery assortment.
“For the first time, Swedish grocery retail has access to comparable carbon footprints across the food assortment, calculated according to a common methodology. This gives the industry a shared starting point to understand climate impact, prioritise action and strengthen climate reporting," says Jenny Hagberg, Head of Sustainability, Swedish Food Retailers’ Federation.
FoodFacts automates the calculation process by combining product information, including ingredients, packaging and geographical origin, with scientifically based life cycle data. This enables more than 120,000 product level footprints to be calculated and continuously updated, rather than relying on broad category averages. Two products in the same category can therefore have different footprints reflecting their individual composition and characteristics.
The current calculations primarily use secondary and representative life cycle data, enabling consistent coverage at scale. As more specific producer data becomes available, it can be incorporated within the same calculation, creating a pathway towards increasingly precise product footprints.
“Agreeing a common methodology is a major step, but applying it across more than 100,000 constantly changing products requires technology. FoodFacts turns that methodology into actionable climate data at scale, with the potential to incorporate increasingly specific producer data over time," says Alexandra Ferreira, CEO at FoodFacts.

This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, said: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”

items.title: Veesion raids Nedap Retail to bring in Wouter Ubbels as retail security firm's VP of Indirect & Mid-Market
items.summary: Veesion, which taps AI to help retailers detect gestures commonly linked to shoplifting, has appointed Wouter Ubbels as Vice President, Indirect and Mid-Market. He will lead the company’s mid-market business and channel partnerships, supporting Veesion’s expansion in the US and internationally.
items.body:
Veesion, which taps AI to help retailers detect gestures commonly linked to shoplifting, has appointed Wouter Ubbels as Vice President, Indirect and Mid-Market.
He will lead the company’s mid-market business and channel partnerships, supporting Veesion’s expansion in the US and internationally. Ubbels joins from Nedap Retail, where he spent nearly 14 years and most recently served as Vice President of Global Sales. His previous positions at Nedap included Director of Channel Sales Americas, with responsibility for partner relationships across North and Latin America.
“Retailers want partners they can trust, and Wouter has spent his career earning that trust on both sides of the Atlantic. We are thrilled to have him lead this next chapter of our growth with mid-market retailers and our partners,” says Veesion Co-founder and CEO Thibault David.
“Mid-market retailers and our partners are two of the biggest opportunities for Veesion. I’m here to make sure both get the attention, support and clarity they need to grow with us,” says Ubbels.
Veesion’s AI analyses video from the cameras a store already has. When it spots gestures commonly linked to shoplifting, it sends a short video alert to store teams. They then review the alerts and decide how to respond.

items.body:
Alan Hoe is starting a new position as Head of Customer Experience & Operations at Marks and Spencer.
His CV includes a 21 year stint at Waitrose & Partners where he held a number of roles during that time, including Retail Proposition Lead - Front End and Services.
Most recently he has been working as a consultant for customer experience consultancy CLX.
It's Christmas!!!
M&S is bringing fashion, home, beauty and food together in one Christmas campaign for the first time since 2017.
The retailer's Home of Christmas offering launches on its Instagram page and YouTube channel at 7am today and stars James Norton as an undercover Santa, alongside Lucy Punch as Mrs. Claus, with a special appearance and exclusive soundtrack by Katherine Jenkins.
Beyond the film, an integrated campaign will run across TV, video on demand, cinema, outdoor, social media, radio, digital display and print, alongside M&S’s owned channels, influencer activity and PR.
Across social and digital channels, the Friends of M&S will share their festive selections through M&S Love That Lists, featuring gifts, food, fashion, beauty and homeware. Customers will also be able to access festive recipes through a hub and check ingredient and product availability through a digital catalogue, supporting meal planning and shopping list preparation.
Sharry Cramond, Fashion, Home & Beauty Marketing Director at M&S, says: "Customers don't think about Christmas as one meal, one gift or one outfit. They think about all the moments that make the season special. As the only retailer with a truly cross-category offer spanning Food, Fashion, Beauty, Gifting and Home, M&S plays a unique role in helping customers create Christmas from start to finish. Bringing those categories together allows us to tell one connected Christmas story and celebrate all the ways our customers make the season their own. That's why we're proud that customers call M&S The Home of Christmas."
Andrew Hicks, Food Marketing Director at M&S, says: "Christmas is made up of countless moments, traditions and rituals that mean something different to every family. For generations, M&S has been privileged to play a part in those celebrations, helping customers create a Christmas that feels uniquely their own."
"From the food shared around the table to the thoughtful finishing touches that make the season memorable, we're proud to be part of some of the moments that matter most. This year's campaign brings that to life in a way that is warm, unexpected and full of charm, celebrating the special place M&S holds in our customers' festive traditions and reinforcing why we're proud to be The Home of Christmas."

items.summary: Katherine Jenkins popped up at London's St. Pancras International on Friday to give people a live performance.The Welsh mezzo-soprano performed her reimagining of Belinda Carlisle's number one song Heaven Is a Place on Earth, which features as the official soundtrack to Marks & Spencer's 20
items.body:
Katherine Jenkins popped up at London's St. Pancras International on Friday to give people a live performance.
The Welsh mezzo-soprano performed her reimagining of Belinda Carlisle's number one song Heaven Is a Place on Earth, which features as the official soundtrack to Marks & Spencer's 2026 Home of Christmas campaign.
Performing beneath St. Pancras International's Christmas tree, which this year is inspired by a traditional German Christmas Pyramid, Jenkins surprised passengers and visitors with three songs, whilst staff from M&S' in-station store handed out festive treats to mark the occasion.
She says: “It was a real joy to see the smile on people’s faces as the performance got underway, and particularly special to sing my new track under the beautiful Christmas tree at St. Pancras International. There's something so wonderful about surprising people and bringing a piece of Christmas magic to their day, and it certainly felt like a fitting time and place to do that.”
Peter Martin-Jones, Head of Marketing at St. Pancras International, says: “Music has always been part of the magic of St. Pancras International, and never more so than at Christmas. We’re thrilled Katherine has brought her extraordinary voice to the station for this special surprise performance, hot on the heels of the M&S Christmas advert, and we hope her performance under our tree has brought festive cheer to many."
