items.title: KPMG UK: consumers holding back purchases for Black Friday promotions
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Half of shoppers searching for Black Friday deals say they have delayed buying items in the hope of seeing them discounted. KPMG surveyed 3000 people across the UK about their intentions for this month’s promotional period that leads up to Black Friday on the 27th. Three quarters (77%) said that they are planning to, or […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Half of shoppers searching for Black Friday deals say they have delayed buying items in the hope of seeing them discounted.
KPMG surveyed 3000 people across the UK about their intentions for this month’s promotional period that leads up to Black Friday on the 27th. Three quarters (77%) said that they are planning to, or may be tempted to, shop – with 49% of them having held off buying target items until this period.
Of the consumers either planning to or that may shop for Black Friday period discounts:
- A third (30%) plan to buy Christmas gifts, and a fifth (22%) plan to buy for themselves.
- A quarter (25%) may be tempted to buy items for themselves, and a fifth (22%) may be tempted to buy Christmas gifts.
Gen Z (Born after 1996) consumers are the age group most commonly planning to shop for themselves or for Christmas gifts for others this Black Friday period. With 71% saying they have delayed buying in the hope of discounts. Regionally, Londoners are the most likely (across all age groups) to be planning Black Friday purchases (35% for themselves and 46% Christmas gifts).
Adults clothing is the most common target, for 30% across all age groups – rising to half (47%) of Gen Z age. Footwear (20%) and Health and Beauty products (20%) complete the top three categories.
With a prolonged hot summer still in mind, nearly one in 10 (7%) consumers are looking for air con deals, while the same amount are respectively focussed on heater purchases for the more immediate colder months.
Among those (23% of) consumers saying they won’t be buying anything this Black Friday, half (48%) said it’s because they don’t trust that the prices on offer are better than any other time of year.
Commenting on the findings, Linda Ellett, head of consumer and retail for KPMG UK, said: “Retail sales were strong in early summer, and weaker in the latter part. What these results suggest is that at least some demand has been delayed – with savvy consumers awaiting Black Friday period promotions. The conventional Christmas promotional shopping season is also being pulled forward. Both of these things are a respective challenge for retailers – who have to consider the need to compete with rivals, the demand for discounts from consumers, while protecting their margins. And, also, how to keep the spending going right through to Christmas Eve.
“Among consumers saying they won’t buy anything this Black Friday period, half cite a lack of belief that Black Friday discounts are better than any other time of year. Retailers need to be mindful of the ongoing job required to convince this group – especially now that AI tools make price tracking easier.”
One in ten consumers (12%) said they will prompt AI chatbot tools (such as Chat GPT and Gemini) in order to find offers – but the popularity of using AI in this way failed to increase on last year (when it was 15%). However, using AI suggested links from search engines to find promotions grew slightly to 13% from 12% 12 months ago.
Heading directly to a retailer’s website (or app) is the most common way (that 53%) that people will find deals, followed by a third (30%) relying on emails from retailers, and a quarter (25%) heading to stores.
Free delivery (40%) and free returns (22%) remain the most popular ways that consumers say retailers can tempt them into making a purchase. While livestream shopping events were least likely to encourage consumers to buy.
Linda Ellett added: “While the results suggest that AI use by consumers as a way of finding Black Friday discounts has largely failed to increase in popularity, one in ten consumers still plan to search for deals using AI chatbot tools and AI search engine link suggestions, respectively. They also serve as a reminder of the importance of multi-channel strategies for retailers, with physical, online and social all ways that different groups of consumers prefer to shop – and the continued strength of free delivery and returns as a purchasing driver.”

items.title: Swedish snacking brand N!CK’S is on a mission to make better-for-you snacking a whole lot tastier in the UK
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. The future of snacking doesn’t have to mean choosing between what tastes good and what feels good. N!CK’S, the Swedish-born confectionery and snacking brand, is accelerating its UK expansion with a growing retail footprint spanning Morrisons, Ocado and Sainsbury’s, alongside existing listings in Boots and leading fitness clubs including Third Space. The expansion marks a […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
The expansion marks a significant step in the brand’s UK growth ambitions, as demand grows for snacks that combine indulgent taste with more considered nutritional credentials. With its protein wafer bars, N!CK’S is targeting the space between traditional confectionery and functional sports nutrition, offering consumers a more treat-led approach to protein snacking.
At the heart of the expansion are N!CK’S protein wafer bars: a deliciously indulgent snack delivering 10g of protein per 40g bar, with no added sugar. The range comes in five flavours: Chocolate, Vanilla, Orange Chocolate, Hazelnut and Peanut Butter. Founded in 2013 in Sweden by Niclas Luthman, N!CK’S was born from a desire to enjoy chocolate and other sweet treats without compromising on sugar intake. Following a prediabetes diagnosis, Niclas began experimenting with recipes to create delicious products without added sugar. Thousands of experiments later, the brand was established with a mission to close the gap between indulgence and health through food innovation.
That ambition is now fuelling international growth. N!CK’S has built a presence across 15 markets, spanning confectionery, protein bars, ice cream and sweeteners. Its total non-frozen sales grew by 33% between 2023 and 2025, reflecting strong momentum across its confectionery and protein bar portfolio.
The UK represents an exciting next chapter, with N!CK’S looking to reach consumers well beyond the traditional sports nutrition aisle. While protein bars have long been associated with workout routines and performance goals, N!CK’S sees a much bigger opportunity. It exists to make protein an easy, enjoyable part of everyday snacking. Its positioning – great taste comes first, and better-for-you credentials should never mean settling for less.
Alongside its grocery expansion, N!CK’S is building its presence in the out-of-home fitness channel, with a rollout into PureGym planned for December and existing listings at Bannatyne, Fitness First and Third Space. These channels provide further opportunities to reach active consumers looking for convenient snacks that fit around busy lifestyles.
Jesper Mathiasson, (VP of Sales) at N!CK’S, says: “The UK is a hugely exciting market for N!CK’S, and these new retail partnerships are a major step forward in our ambition to make better-for-you snacking more accessible. We believe people should never have to choose between a genuinely delicious treat and making more considered food choices. That’s why we put taste at the heart of everything we do, with no added sugar and protein adding to the appeal. We’re here to shake up the category, bring a little more joy to everyday snacking and show consumers that better-for-you can still be seriously indulgent.”
As the lines between confectionery, everyday snacking and functional nutrition continue to blur, the brand is betting on a simple idea with big potential – that the next generation of better-for-you snacks won’t ask consumers to compromise.

items.title: Digested week: The harrowing backstory to the John Lewis Christmas ad | Emma Brockes
items.summary: Plus, the king’s regret-without-liability statement on slavery, and getting mogged by Collins dictionary All eyes on America as a nation decides, but this week Brits faced an equally large question: namely, how do we feel about this year’s John Lewis Christmas ad? It’s a confusing one. On the one hand, high off her flinty brilliance in six seasons of Slow Horses , Kristin Scott Thomas is a welcome addition to any production and I could watch her waft around a big house without the pretext of either John Lewis or Christmas. Continue reading...
items.body:
Monday
All eyes on America as a nation decides, but this week Brits faced an equally large question: namely, how do we feel about this year’s John Lewis Christmas ad? It’s a confusing one. On the one hand, high off her flinty brilliance in six seasons of Slow Horses, Kristin Scott Thomas is a welcome addition to any production and I could watch her waft around a big house without the pretext of either John Lewis or Christmas.
On the other hand, it’s all a bit odd. The advert’s much discussed storyline in which Scott Thomas’s daughter and son-in-law come to the door with their owl-eyed children doesn’t exactly emanate Christmas spirit, even as the “before” in a before-and-after story.
Why does the grandma appear to have no relationship with her grandkids? Has there been a massive fight in the family? If there has, is it about new inheritance tax rules and how they might push Christmas gift-giving more in the direction of money – deed transfer, not 20 quid in an envelope – over presents? Has the Scott Thomas character raised the possibility that she doesn’t trust her family to look out for her if she puts her house in their name, and have they shot back, huffily: “That’s ridiculous, mother, we’d always do right by you, do you really want us to give 40% of your estate to HMRC when there’s a perfectly sensible way around it?” And has she replied, coldly: “Why would I care, I won’t be here.” To which have they replied, in a howl of protest: “We think you’re being very selfish.”
Has she said to them: “Look, I’m already contributing substantially to the school fees after the 20% VAT hike, what more do you want from me?” To which have they replied: “Fine, we’ll pull the kids out of private and send them to state school, but we’ll need money for therapists, so can you please put the house in our name?” To which has she replied, in a deadly escalation: “Vote Reform then if you feel so strongly about inheritance tax,” to which have they replied, absolutely screaming at this point: “How very dare you, we’re on the left!”
To which has she snorted: “Well, I know for a fact that he – pointing to her son-in-law – voted for David Cameron at least once,” to which has her daughter exploded: “Ohmigod, says the woman who voted for Brexit!” At this point has her son-in-law walked quietly over to the wall and mimed beating his head against it? Does she even want them there for Christmas? Is that why the kids are so sullen? Is this who we are as a people now and has it fallen to John Lewis to tell us?
Tuesday
A rigorous workout for our nerves, as we look towards the US midterms and try to avoid tempting fate by saying words like “landslide”, “got this”, or “win” ahead of time. For reasons of self-preservation, my assumption is that Donald Trump’s poor approval ratings will somehow resolve themselves at the 11th hour and hand us a fudge of a result, allowing him to stagger on.
This anticipatory hedge is bolstered by British TV news hacks who, almost to a person, manage to find the most lunatic anomalies in any voter set to share with the viewers back home. A Texan of Mexican origin who has lost family members to brutal deportation raids by ICE but still intends to vote for Trump? Tick. A well-to-do family appalled by Elon Musk’s efforts to buy the election and stick a huge datacentre next to their house, but for whom the top voting priority is the question of gender identity and will be voting for Trump, too? Yup. A sense of Americans-say-the-funniest-things animating most foreign reporting? That, too.
Wednesday
King Charles visits the Caribbean and issues a regret-without-liability statement around Britain’s role in the slave trade, but it’s his hissy fit at not having an umbrella that catches my eye. This petulant side to the king is one we haven’t seen in full glory since his meltdown, four years ago, over a leaky fountain pen at a signing ceremony, and I couldn’t enjoy it more.
Then, Charles popped out of his chair, paced the room irritably and snapped, “I can’t bear this bloody thing! Every stinking time!” while Camilla staunched the flow of ink and calmly got on with her own signing. In this week’s incident, the king, caught in a sudden downpour at an outside ceremony in Antigua, gesticulates wildly and with a furious stream of what we might assume to be invective, looks sharply around for someone to hand him an umbrella. Camilla, meanwhile, grips her own umbrella and beetles off, stage right, leaving her other half to compose himself and remind the rest of us of the endearing normalcy of royalty – or how our social order enables and forgives adult tantrums, depending on one’s view.
Thursday
New threshold crossed! For the first time the word of the year from one of the big dictionaries is a word I haven’t encountered. I don’t know what this means but it’s probably not good. Either that, or “mogging” isn’t quite as widely used as Collins suggests. Apparently it’s a term taken from bodybuilding and applied to people one-upping each other on the internet, as in, per the dictionary’s explanation, “your friend’s sourdough mogs the loaf you spent all weekend proving”.
I mean – and I know this is what happens when you age out of exposure to new idioms – it sounds totally made up to me, like something from an old episode of Brass Eye, specifically the one about deprived youths loading pensioners into shopping trolleys and “git-surfing” them round the estate.
Friday
Almost a week on from Martha Stewart’s disastrous choice of Halloween costume and it’s worth a revisit to remind us just how enjoyably poor her decision-making was. After dressing as a homeless person with a sign around her neck reading “I am hungry. Please help!” the 85-year-old had to apologise, although you could tell she wasn’t happy about it and later came up with the claim that she had only worn it because someone spilled chocolate on her “other” costume. Hilariously unconvincing from Martha, and I couldn’t love her more.

JD has unveiled its Christmas 2026 campaign, “Create the New,” bringing together a diverse lineup of artists, musicians, athletes and emerging creatives for a celebration of the next generation shaping culture. Building on the global retailer’s “Forever Forward” platform, the campaign challenges the traditional idea of Christmas as a time to slow down. Instead, JD […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
JD has unveiled its Christmas 2026 campaign, “Create the New,” bringing together a diverse lineup of artists, musicians, athletes and emerging creatives for a celebration of the next generation shaping culture.
Building on the global retailer’s “Forever Forward” platform, the campaign challenges the traditional idea of Christmas as a time to slow down. Instead, JD is turning its attention towards a generation that sees the end of the year as an opportunity to build momentum, embrace new possibilities and get ahead of what’s next.
Underpinned by the creative messages “Do What’s Never Been Done” and “It’s not the end. It’s a warm-up.”, “Create the New” offers a fresh perspective on the festive season, placing ambition, self-expression and cultural progression at the centre of its narrative.
At the heart of the campaign is a new hero film, bringing together talent from sport, music, fashion and entertainment. Reflecting JD’s connection to contemporary youth culture, the film serves as the centrepiece of a wider campaign designed to celebrate the people and communities influencing the future.
Bringing together the next generation of cultural talent
Music plays a central role in “Create the New” and is soundtracked by a classic anthem currently trending on EU dancefloors and UK club nights. Not Over Yet performed by Grace and Paul Oakenfold plays whilst JD brings together some of the UK’s most exciting names from across the electronic music scene, alongside sporting stars and young creatives.
Among the campaign’s leading figures are Sammy Virji, Josh Baker and Chris Stassy, three artists helping shape the sound of contemporary dance music, alongside emerging DJ Kai Saunders.
Their involvement reflects JD’s growing relationship with electronic music culture, recognising the communities, creative spaces and emerging movements that continue to influence fashion and youth identity.
Joining them are singer-songwriter Skye Newman and streamer favourites Bov Boys. From the world of women’s football, we see Lauren James and custom football jacket designer, Antonia Bronze. Creatives such as graphic designer, Che and director, Frankie Spence further expand the campaign’s flow and provide a stage for emerging talent.
The lineup brings together individuals from different disciplines, each representing a distinct part of contemporary culture while sharing a commitment to originality and progression.
Beyond the UK, “Create the New” also features an international cast of talent, including Spanish footballer and World Cup-winning goal scorer Ferran Torres (SP), mixed martial artist Ilia Topuria (SP), YouTube Streamer Plex (SP) and internationally acclaimed artists Emelia Mernes (AR), Ele A (CH), Ronisia (FR) and Ino Casablanca (FR).
Together, the lineup reflects JD’s international presence and its ability to connect communities across different countries, creative disciplines and cultural backgrounds. The campaign brings these worlds together through a shared attitude towards creativity, ambition and what comes next.
Speaking of the campaign, Paul Orange, managing director at JD said: “JD has always been shaped by the communities at the heart of sport, music and style. With ‘Create the New’, we’re celebrating a generation that is making its own opportunities and taking culture forward. Christmas is a moment to come together, and we want this campaign to capture the energy and ambition of young people who are already thinking about what comes next. It’s that attitude that drives ‘Forever Forward’ and our commitment to giving the next generation a platform.”
A new perspective on Christmas
While traditional Christmas campaigns often focus on nostalgia, familiar rituals and the anticipation of the festive break, “Create the New” takes a different approach.
For the generation at the centre of JD’s campaign, the closing months of the year are an opportunity to continue creating, connecting and moving forward.
This philosophy runs throughout the campaign, from its talent selection and London-shot creative to its wider message of challenging expectations and refusing to stand still.
The campaign also places footwear and apparel at the forefront, highlighting the role of personal style in the communities JD represents.
As the latest expression of JD’s “Forever Forward” platform, “Create the New” reinforces the retailer’s commitment to celebrating the next generation of cultural voices, championing individuality and bringing together communities united by a desire to push boundaries.
JD’s Christmas 2026 campaign, “Create the New”, launches globally on 6 November 2026.

items.body:
New data reveals 45% of Wickes Community Programme applications now come from schools, nurseries and PTAs, with more than 60% seeking support to improve outdoor environments
As schools across the UK celebrate Outdoor Classroom Day on Thursday 5th November, new data from the Wickes Community Programme reveals growing demand for better outdoor learning environments, with nearly half (45%) of all funding and material requests now coming from schools, nurseries and PTAs.
Outdoor Classroom Day is a global campaign held twice a year, in May and November, which encourages teachers to take learning outside through play, exploration and practical activities. The campaign aims to make outdoor learning part of children’s everyday experiences, rather than something reserved for special occasions.
Reflecting this growing interest, more than 60% of educational applications to the Wickes Community Programme seek support to improve outdoor spaces, including nature hubs, sensory gardens, allotments and outdoor play areas.
Two recent projects in Woodborough and Southampton demonstrate how schools and local Wickes teams are bringing these ideas to life, from extensive playground transformations to finding new uses for materials that would otherwise go to waste.
Woodborough CE Primary School
To support more opportunities for outdoor learning and play, Woodborough CE Primary School has completed an extensive transformation of its grounds through the Outdoor Play and Learning (OPAL) programme.
Working alongside DIY content creator Aimee (@TheCountryReno), and with material donations from Wickes, including raised planters, a playhouse and an apex shed, the school has brought pupils’ wishlist to life. The transformed space includes water stations, vegetable beds and loose-parts play zones, giving children more opportunities to explore, play and learn outdoors.
The project reflects the spirit of Outdoor Classroom Day, which encourages schools to make the most of their outdoor environments and give children more opportunities to learn through practical, hands-on experiences.
Mrs Freya Wren, Headteacher at Woodborough CE Primary, said: “Our enhanced OPAL provision gives children the freedom to explore, take managed risks, solve problems together, and develop confidence and resilience. The new spaces encourage curiosity, collaboration and enjoyment. We are incredibly proud of what our school community has achieved and grateful to our families, Aimee and the Wickes Community Programme for supporting our vision.”
Southampton school
In Southampton, a local Wickes store has found a practical way to support a school’s new forest school and mud kitchen, while also making use of materials that would otherwise have been discarded.
When the school needed secure storage for its outdoor learning equipment, the Southampton team repurposed pallets, non-returnable timber spacers and damaged fence panels to hand-build two heavy-duty storage units. The materials were given a new lease of life, providing the school with a practical solution to safely store its tools and resources.
Hannah Randle Hockin, Community Engagement and Social Impact Manager at Wickes, said: “Every school has different needs, and sometimes it’s the smallest things that can make the biggest difference. Whether it’s helping to transform an outdoor space with new planters and play equipment, or finding a new use for materials that would otherwise go to waste, we’re proud to support schools and communities with practical solutions that help bring their ideas to life.”
Schools, charities, and community groups seeking material donations or assistance for their outdoor learning spaces can apply through the Wickes Community Programme by visiting www.wickes.co.uk/communityprogramme.

What will people be drinking next? Oatly, the world’s original and largest oat drink company, has published its second Future of Taste report. items.body:
What will people be drinking next? Oatly, the world’s original and largest oat drink company, has published its second Future of Taste report. It brings together more than 200 interviews with baristas, café owners, mixologists and drinks experts across 21 countries, alongside quantitative trends data compiled by researchers CultureLab, to identify the trends expected to shape café menus in the coming months.
The report points to a potential overhaul of coffee menus on the horizon, with a growing interest in botanical and fermented ingredients, a boom in non-coffee and tea orders, and – with the rise of innovations like coffee jelly – “texture” playing an increasingly starring role.
Rowena Roos, Oatly Head of FADE said:
“This year’s Future of Taste Report makes one thing very clear: people are expecting a lot more from their drinks. They want more excitement, more texture, and more functionality. From wellness drinks with real personality to global flavours, playful textures and cafés at the core of actual human connection, menus are becoming far more expressive. It’s been exciting to hear how many creators see oat drink as a brilliant starting point for that creativity, allowing baristas and café teams to build drinks people don’t just order but remember.”
THE PHARMAFICATION OF DRINKS: Herbs, botanicals and fermented ingredients are moving further into everyday drinks, as cafés borrow from wellness, nature and traditional food cultures. 40% of drinks professionals say herbs and botanicals will shape the future of flavour, making them the number one taste trend in the report. Ginger, hibiscus and lavender are among the ingredients gaining attention, while 56% of experts spontaneously mentioned fermentation. Alongside kombucha, drinks such as tepache, kvass and Turkish şalgam are starting to appear on the radar.
“We did a green bean tepache a couple of months ago – pineapple fermented with green coffee beans into a kombucha-esque ferment, which we did with tonic and cold brew. It was so wacky but so fun. People either loved it or hated it, but they went for it and they tried it. – Flo Thomas, Batch Baby, London
Olive Sour: Salty olives and brine mix with refreshing lemon and vegetable juice. Topped with an olive oil Oatly Barista Cold Foam.
THE GREAT CAFÉ RECONNECTION: With the rise of AI and at-home working, cafés are taking on a bigger role as places to meet, spend time and find community. 51% of drinks experts say belonging, community or connection will be central to the future of cafés. That could mean specialist coffee communities, matcha groups, music-led spaces or cafés built around other shared interests. The drink still matters, but increasingly, so does what happens around it.
“AI is going to take over people’s desktops, and a lot of people are working remotely. There’ll come a day where a lot of people go the whole day and only speak to AI. The way we’ve evolved, we need real experiences – people are going to want real things. It might be the one human interaction they have in a day.” – Sooji Im, Founder of Tokkia, London
Goji Mont Blanc
Iced filter with sweet and tangy goji berry syrup, topped with Oatly Barista Cold Foam. The classic format reinvented with a twist.
THE END OF THE FLAT WHITE? Coffee and tea are no longer the only drinks competing for space on the café menu. 82% of baristas and café owners mentioned drinks that were neither tea nor coffee. Ube was mentioned twice as often as the flat white or cappuccino, while refreshers, botanical sodas, fermented drinks, hojicha, coconut and hibiscus are also finding their way onto menus. The result is a café menu that looks increasingly different from the one we’re used to.
“If I go to a café, I still have my flat white or batch brew. But if I see an interesting refresher-style soda, I will always order that as well as my coffee, and a lot of younger people are starting to have a similar attitude.” – Ollie Baumber, Clifton Coffee Roasters, Bristol
Coconut Pandan Cloud
Coconut, espresso and orange blossom water meld together with the floral and coconutty notes of the pandan Oatly Cold Foam. Floral, bitter, creamy and very definitely not your usual latte.
THE SQUISHY BOOM: For many drinkers, flavour is only part of the appeal. Texture and appearance are becoming part of the order too. 72% of beverage experts say mouthfeel is becoming as important as flavour. Jelly, foam, fizz, chewy toppings, fruit pieces and layered drinks are all part of this shift. Looks matter too, with 37% of experts saying how a drink looks is integral to its appeal. Whilst, google searches for coffee jelly are up 90% year-on-year globally.
“I think people feel texture a lot more than they even realise. And not just mouthfeel – the feel of the glass in your hand, the salt rim, the feel on your lips as well as in your mouth.” – Rebecca Morgan Lewis, Origin Coffee Roasters, London
Pannoat Cotta Thai Tea
A thick slurpable pannoat cotta made with Oatly Barista Edition Coconut Flavour is the base of this texture rich beverage. Topped with a creamy Thai tea mix.
The findings build on Oatly’s 2025 Future of Taste report, which correctly identified the rise of decaf, the proliferation of fiber-focused drinks and the staying power of matcha beyond a passing fad.
Read the full report at: oatly.com/future-of-taste
View Oatly’s Lookbook – our take on upcoming trends and recipes – here: oatly.com/lookbook

Co-op Wholesale has officially launched a new Nisa store in Smallfield (Horley), Surrey. It is now open to the public serving a wide selection of award-winning Co-op Brand lines as well as other popular convenience goods.
Located on Woodbridge Chapel Road, the new convenience store has benefited from a full fit out of the new Nisa proposition. Standing at 2,000sqft, it is set up to serve customers in the picturesque village.
Amrit Bhandal will operate the store serving the residential area with vital food, drinks and snacks as well as housing some additional and unique offerings. A Costa coffee station will cater to customers wanting to caffeinate on the go, while those looking for the latest cold drink trends will be delighted to find Isqueez blend milkshake machine, and a Skwishee slushy machine onsite. Hot food and an instore bakery occupy prime positions too, ready to serve shoppers looking for food for now options throughout the day, which are supplied by Country Choice.
The new store gives local shoppers access to a wide range of everyday essentials, fresh food and Co-op brand products, offering them quality, value and convenience. Among the 2,400+ Co-op brand lines available to all Nisa symbols to stock are fresh and chilled, food-to-go, fresh produce, frozen and award-winning premium ranges, under the Irresistible moniker.
Nisa stores uniquely benefit from having access to the Co-op brand, which brings a wealth of benefit to independent retailers’ customers, from recognisable products that fit their lifestyle to solutions for any meal or snacking occasion. Nisa retailers also receive far-reaching support from Co-op Wholesale teams, encompassing operations, supply chain, marketing and more to support the running of their independent business.
Ian King, Business Development and Growth Director at Co-op Wholesale, commented: “The opening of this new Horley store is a great opportunity for the retailer and a positive addition to the local convenience market. With a strong location on Chapel Road and an offer tailored to the needs of local customers, the store is well positioned for success. We’re excited to support the team on their journey.”
Amrit Bhandal, Owner of Nisa Horley, commented: “Opening this new Nisa store is an exciting milestone for our business. We’ve invested in creating a modern, convenient shopping destination for local people and look forward to serving the Horley community for many years to come.”
Making a difference in the Community (MADL)
A unique point of difference and real draw for Nisa stores is Co-op Wholesale’s charity – Making A Difference Locally (MADL). It supports retail partners through fundraising via Co-op brand products’ sales to support causes local to stores.

items.title: Black Friday spending to hit £6.7 billion as shoppers delay purchases for discounts
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. As households look to make Christmas budgets stretch further, shoppers are taking an increasingly strategic approach to festive spending. New research commissioned by PayPal reveals consumers have been deliberately postponing major purchases and are using Black Friday as a key opportunity to stretch Christmas budgets further, with spending across Black Friday and Cyber Monday estimated […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
As households look to make Christmas budgets stretch further, shoppers are taking an increasingly strategic approach to festive spending.
New research commissioned by PayPal reveals consumers have been deliberately postponing major purchases and are using Black Friday as a key opportunity to stretch Christmas budgets further, with spending across Black Friday and Cyber Monday estimated to reach £6.7 billion1 this year.
Black Friday shoppers are taking an increasingly strategic approach to festive spending, with almost half (48%) admitting to waiting two months or more for a specific item in this year’s sales.3
To illustrate the purchases driving Black Friday spending this year, PayPal has created a “Black Friday Basket” featuring some of the most popular items shoppers hope to buy during the sales. The basket also reflects how the event has increasingly become a planned opportunity to make Christmas budgets go further.
Beauty and fragrance products top consumers’ wish lists (44%), followed by fashion and trainers (39%), toys (38%), Christmas decorations (30%) and holiday bookings (27%). Larger purchases such as mobile phones (22%), laptops or tablets (20%), games consoles (20%) and smartwatches (20%) also feature on shopping lists.
Almost half (45%) of Brits say they are planning to shop the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales this year, and as households look to balance festive spending with ongoing cost pressures, many are also turning to more flexible ways to pay like PayPal Pay in 3 and Pay in 30 Days.
While debit cards remain the most popular choice for shoppers’ Black Friday purchases (30%), 12% plan to use digital wallets such as PayPal and almost one in ten (9%) intend to use Buy Now, Pay Later services (from any provider)4.
The research suggests that, as part of the mix of options available to them, consumers are combining discounts with a range of ways to pay in the run-up to Christmas.
Dave Jones, head of UK consumer at PayPal said, “Black Friday has increasingly become one of the biggest moments in the festive shopping calendar, as shoppers look for ways to make their money go further. Payment flexibility is becoming just as important as finding the right deal, and some are considering a range of options, including Buy Now, Pay Later, alongside traditional payment methods.
“Many shoppers want three things: value, flexibility and control. They’re planning ahead and waiting for discounts on the items they want and choosing payment options that fit their budget. Whether that’s paying upfront, using a digital wallet or, where it is affordable, spreading the cost over time, consumers are taking a more deliberate approach to how they shop during the festive season.”
With the rise in everyday costs, Black Friday has become a more planned moment for many households, with some shoppers becoming more selective about how they buy and pay.
The PayPal Black Friday Basket highlights the categories consumers are most hoping to secure deals on this year, spanning everything from beauty and fragrance products to fashion, toys, technology and holiday bookings.
Following the UK’s hottest summer on record, almost 5 million Brits5 are planning to buy an air conditioning unit or fan.
The top 10 categories shoppers say they are hoping to buy:
- Beauty or fragrance (44%)
- Fashion or trainers (39%)
- Toys (38%)
- Christmas decorations (30%)
- Holiday or travel bookings (27%)
- Gaming accessories (25%)
- Headphones or earbuds (23%)
- Mobile phone (22%)
- Other kitchen appliances (22%)

items.body:
British shoppers are set to make every pound count this festive season as AliExpress launches its biggest-ever UK shopping event, with coupon savings up to 20% off on top of sale prices. The international online retail marketplace is celebrating this year’s 11.11 Global Shopping Festival with curated tech and branded products that deliver real value, running from 1st November to 3rd December. Shoppers will discover spec-led products with competitive pricing and significant savings, proving you don’t need to compromise on quality to shop smart.
This year, AliExpress has extended the 11.11 sales period – its longest yet – so shoppers can take time to browse and research products and deals across an even longer window, covering 11.11, Black Friday and Cyber Monday in one continuous promotional season. UK shoppers could unlock up to 20% off using platform coupons on top of product discounts, plus additional PayPal benefits.*
- 11.11 Sale: 1–18 November
- Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sale: 19th November–3rd December
Brand+ channel celebrates one year
AliExpress Brand+ celebrates one year of bringing the best tech and innovation to UK consumers. The curated range features branded products from over 2,000 brands including Xiaomi, Anker, Li-Ning, Xtep, Lefant, FIFINE, WOLFBOX, THINKCAR, Super Run, all offering exclusive deals throughout the 11.11 shopping festival.
AliExpress will continue to offer price matches for selected items, with products carrying the Best Price Guarantee label, against e-commerce platforms including Amazon, eBay, Temu and Shein, refunding the difference if found cheaper elsewhere within seven days of purchase*.
Finch Li, general manager at AliExpress UK, said: “British shoppers are among the most discerning in the world – they want quality, they want choice, and they want value. That’s why we’ve focused on bringing the latest products and brands to the UK market, with spec-led items that compete on performance and price. With the festive season approaching, we know shoppers are planning carefully and our 11.11 festival is the perfect opportunity to discover everything from considerate gifts to everyday essentials. This year, we’re making it bigger – and better value – than ever.”
Upgraded logistics and customer experiences
This year, AliExpress has transformed with a stronger focus on user experience and faster delivery. Through Local+, more products are shipped from UK warehouses and typically delivered within 1-3 days, while cross-border parcels generally arrive in 7-10 days.
The biggest savings are concentrated in consumer electronics and tech — categories where UK shoppers are most price-sensitive. From audiophile-grade earphones at highly favourable prices to smart home devices compatible with major ecosystems, the campaign argues that British shoppers need not pay a premium for quality.
Ahead of 11.11, AliExpress reports growing demand in branded and AI-powered products
Sales through the Brand+ channel now account for a growing share of total UK sales on AliExpress, demonstrating the appetite of UK consumers for branded, quality products on the platform. The channel has achieved a 65% repeat purchase rate, with nearly two-thirds of customers returning for more branded purchases.
Steady demand for branded products has been complemented by a key trend in 2026: the growing popularity of AliExpress’s AI-powered electronics and gadgets. These have seen a remarkable 100% year-on-year increase in cross-border sales from January to July 2026 compared to the prior year. AI-capability enhancement products like computer processors and mini-PCs , smart home gadgets have dominated the sales chart for months on the platform. AliExpress is quickly becoming the go-to platform for AI-powered brands, ranging from smart home to note-taking devices.

To celebrate the opening, customers had the chance to get their ‘paws’ on 100 limited-edition goody bags and spin Jollyes’ iconic ‘Wheel of Fur-tune’ for a chance to win prizes.
The new 5,800 square foot store officially opened with Provost Jim Leishman on hand to cut the ribbon and welcome the first customers between 9.30-10.30am, alongside a special guest appearance from Dunfermline’s best loved bear, Sammy the Tammy from Dunfermline AFC fame. Scotland national piper Louise Marshall also attended to give a true Scottish welcome to new shoppers.
Customers are now able to browse much loved household names including Pedigree, Whiskas, Harringtons and Felix, alongside specialist pet brands such as Royal Canin and Hill’s, giving pet parents even more choice when it comes to finding the right products for their furry family members.
The store also stocks Jollyes Pets own label ranges, including Lifestage for dogs and cats and Optimum Pet Health, offering big-brand quality at own label prices and backed by a 100% money back guarantee.
Pet parents can also expect an extensive selection of raw food, natural treats and fresh food, alongside toys, treats and accessories, all under one roof.
The opening has created eight new jobs in the local community and the store is led by store manager, Andi Glass.
Andi Glass, store manager at Jollyes Pets Dunfermline, said: “I’m absolutely delighted to have opened the new Dunfermline store and to welcome local pet owners and their four-legged friends through our doors. As a proud dog owner myself, with my Staffie/Husky, Shelby keeping me on my toes, I know just how important it is to find the right products to keep our pets happy, healthy and entertained!”
“We’re especially excited to be able to lower pet costs for the people of Dunfermline and their furry friends. I’m really looking forward to meeting the local community and their pets, as well as leading our fantastic team in delivering great service and brilliant value for pet owners across Fife”.

items.title: Build visibility and reach more shoppers this Christmas
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. The Christmas season creates opportunities far beyond product promotion. Editorial features, engaging content and memorable customer experiences give retailers powerful ways to reach audiences, build brand affinity and support sales. PR Suite sets out five actions to strengthen visibility during this key trading period. Christmas PR is underway Christmas editorial is planned well ahead, but […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
The Christmas season creates opportunities far beyond product promotion. Editorial features, engaging content and memorable customer experiences give retailers powerful ways to reach audiences, build brand affinity and support sales. PR Suite sets out five actions to strengthen visibility during this key trading period.
Christmas PR is underway
Christmas editorial is planned well ahead, but media need relevant stories right through to the final shopping days. Look beyond broad gifting categories to niche recipients, specific occasions and practical shopping needs. Consider instantly accessible gifts, such as digital presents, and last-minute appointment availability, from beauty services to festive treatments.
Put value into context through budget-led selections, useful bundles and complimentary services. Share relevant offers with shopping editors, including clear pricing, promotional dates and availability. Highlight extended opening hours, gift cards, delivery cut-offs and immediate collection.
Supply purchasing links and high-resolution photography, including product cut-outs or shots on white backgrounds. Match each angle to the right contact and confirm they’re still accepting submissions.
Sell the occasion through the story
Bring products to life through Christmas storytelling. Develop Christmas cocktail recipes, party-season hair tutorials, festive home decorating ideas, hosting guides and advice on choosing a thoughtful guest gift.
Use expert commentary, recipe cards and visual demonstrations across your website and social content. Pitch relevant ideas to media as advice-led features, giving each story a clear audience and a practical application.
Make your products discoverable through AI
AI search tools can draw on retailer websites, editorial features and independent reviews to answer shopping questions. A product page supplies the facts; a gift guide or review can explain suitability and provide an independent assessment. Both owned and earned media can become sources for product discovery.
Strengthen that opportunity with descriptions that explain benefits, recipients, budgets and occasions. Keep information consistent across retail listings and provide accurate details for journalists’ coverage. Work with your website team to ensure important pages can be found and indexed.
Create content your customers are already asking for
Questions from shop floors, website enquiries and social comments reveal what matters to your customers and where they need more information. Turn recurring requests into editorial angles, engaging guides and demonstrations.
Build these answers into your social channels, newsletters and website content. Make product-led social posts easy to shop with clear prices and direct purchasing links. Demonstrate products in use and share timely offers, loyalty benefits and savings with the details customers need to act. Offer relevant insights to editors and host live sessions where people can ask questions and engage directly with your team.
Turn Christmas visitors into lasting customer relationships
Christmas is retail’s busiest trading season. Make that footfall count by setting your team up for success. Prepare colleagues with the knowledge and support to deliver an exceptional customer experience. Your people and your store should leave shoppers with a lasting impression of what makes your brand worth returning to.
Give customers a reason to visit beyond shopping. Create a Christmas experience that brings your brand to life, whether it’s a small, thoughtful touch or a bigger festive event. This could be as simple as gift wrapping, personalisation, styling appointments or festive tastings. A pet store could host Santa on December Saturdays, while a children’s clothing store could create a Christmas photo booth for families. Promote these experiences through local media and listings to give shoppers another reason to visit.
Kaytlyn Mitchell, founder & CEO of PR Suite, said: “Christmas creates a concentrated period of consumer attention, but visibility shouldn’t depend on seasonal promotions alone. Retailers have opportunities across their products, expertise, people and customer experiences to create stories that audiences and media find useful.
“The strongest approach connects those opportunities across earned media, owned content and in-store activity, helping retailers support Christmas sales while building stronger customer relationships beyond Christmas.”

The LEGO Group today opened the doors to its 24th store in the UK. Located in Lakeside shopping centre, the new 217sq m LEGO Store is already delighting fans of all ages, as they gathered excitedly this morning to catch the official opening.
William Johnson, age 9 from Essex, cut the ribbon and then shoppers were treated to impressive builds and exclusive opening offers. The first visitors to the new store also enjoyed LEGO product favourites such as LEGO City, LEGO Friends and LEGO Ninjago, plus LEGO Retail exclusives such as the LEGO Play Station™, LEGO Ideas Downton Abbey and the LEGO Star Wars™ Executor Super Star Destroyer™
Open seven days a week from 5th November, the new LEGO Store features a range of experiences including:
- Unforgettable immersive experiences – including Pick a Brick Wall and Build a Minifigure Tower.
- Exclusive products – the LEGO Store Lakeside will be home to the largest range of LEGO products, including many exclusive sets such as the LEGO Ideas The X-Files set and the LEGO Icons Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku set
- Rewarding offers – guests at the new store will also have the opportunity to collect LEGO Insiders loyalty programme points which can be used for discounts on future purchases or exclusive member offers.
Amy Pearson, senior marketing director, LEGO Retail at the LEGO Group, said: “When we plan a new store location, we look for places where LEGO play can become ingrained in everyday moments – whether that is a family day out, a special celebration or a quick visit that sparks curiosity and excitement. Lakeside felt like a natural fit, and we’re excited to become part of a destination where people already come together to shop, spend time and make memories.”
Nancy Foster, centre director at Lakeside Shopping Centre, commented: “The arrival of the LEGO Store is a brilliant addition to Lakeside’s growing mix of leading retail brands. As one of the world’s most loved brands, the LEGO Group brings something truly special for families, collectors and builders of every age to enjoy together. More than a store, this immersive new space provides another exciting reason to visit Lakeside, reflecting our continued focus on creating a destination where people come together to shop, explore and enjoy experiences beyond shopping.”

items.body:
For the first time since 2017, M&S is bringing Fashion, Home, Beauty and Food together in one Christmas campaign.
The Home of Christmas launches on M&S’s Instagram page and YouTube channel at 7am on Friday 6 November 2026 and stars James Norton as an undercover Santa, alongside Lucy Punch as Mrs. Claus, with a special appearance and exclusive soundtrack by Katherine Jenkins OBE.
The campaign was informed by M&S research highlighting the importance of spending Christmas together. More than four in five M&S customers (81%) want a special Christmas with the people they love, while 57% plan to spend as much time as possible with family and friends. Food is central to those celebrations, with 68% saying it is what makes the season feel special.
Reflecting those priorities, the film follows Santa, played by James Norton, as he leaves the North Pole to experience Christmas for himself. Encouraged by Mrs. Claus, played by Lucy Punch, he swaps his red suit for a Christmas jumper and shaves off his beard to avoid being recognised. Without his familiar appearance, audiences see a more relatable Santa sharing in the traditions and celebrations that take place in homes across the country.
His journey brings together festive meals, gifts, fashion and home, showing the role M&S plays in helping customers prepare for and celebrate the season.
The story is accompanied by Katherine Jenkins’ specially recorded version of Heaven Is a Place on Earth. The campaign song will be released on launch day, extending the soundtrack beyond the film.
Beyond the film, the integrated campaign will run across TV, video on demand, cinema, outdoor, social media, radio, digital display and print, alongside M&S’s owned channels, influencer activity and PR. The activity will bring the same Christmas story to life across Food, Fashion, Home and Beauty.
Across social and digital channels, the Friends of M&S will share their festive selections through M&S Love That Lists, featuring gifts, food, fashion, beauty and homeware. Customers will also be able to access festive recipes through the M&S Recipe Hub and check ingredient and product availability through the M&S Digital Catalogue, supporting meal planning and shopping-list preparation.
Sharry Cramond, fashion, home & beauty marketing director at M&S, said: “Customers don’t think about Christmas as one meal, one gift or one outfit. They think about all the moments that make the season special. As the only retailer with a truly cross-category offer spanning Food, Fashion, Beauty, Gifting and Home, M&S plays a unique role in helping customers create Christmas from start to finish. Bringing those categories together allows us to tell one connected Christmas story and celebrate all the ways our customers make the season their own. That’s why we’re proud that customers call M&S The Home of Christmas.”
Andrew Hicks, Food Marketing Director at M&S, said: “Christmas is made up of countless moments, traditions and rituals that mean something different to every family. This year’s campaign brings that to life in a way that is warm, unexpected and full of charm, celebrating the special place M&S holds in our customers’ festive traditions and reinforcing why we’re proud to be The Home of Christmas.”

items.title: Hampshire shoplifter gets eight-month jail term
items.summary: A shoplifter has been jailed for 34 weeks after he stole items worth more than £675 from convenience stores in Aldershot, Hampshire. The sentence reflects a growing determination from courts to crack down on shoplifting. Shaun Mason, 39, of Barn Avenue, Aldershot, stole drinks, confectionery,… This story continues at Hampshire shoplifter gets eight-month jail term Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The sentence reflects a growing determination from courts to crack down on shoplifting.
Shaun Mason, 39, of Barn Avenue, Aldershot, stole drinks, confectionery, food and laundry products worth £575 from One Stop on North Lane between June and October.
He also stole ice-cream, drinks and confectionery worth £104 from Co-op on North Lane between June and October.
Basingstoke Magistrates Court also heard he assaulted a female staff member and damaged glass bottles of alcohol worth £36 at the Co-op in June.
Officers arrested Mason and charged him with 16 counts of theft from a shop, common assault, criminal damage and breaking bail conditions.
He pleaded guilty to all offences and was jailed for 34 weeks at Basingstoke Magistrates Court this week (3 November).
Mason was also given a 12-month restraining order, which has banned him from entering the Co-op on North Lane.
Police sergeant Rob Tiller said: “We know Shaun Mason’s behaviour has had a huge impact on businesses, shop workers and the wider community.
“We take all reports of shoplifting extremely seriously and I hope this result reassures the local community that we will do all we can to put offenders before the courts.
“We want to stop this type of behaviour, and encourage businesses affected to please keep reporting crimes to us so we can relentlessly pursue those responsible.
“If you are a shop owner or staff member, please continue to report any shopliftings to us.
“With your information, we can take action, including arresting and charging suspects and convicting offenders at court.”

items.title: Co-op Group and Southern Co-op receive final CMA approval
items.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has given complete approval for the merger of the Co-op Group and Southern Co-op, marking a major milestone for the businesses. This comes after…
items.body:
Co-op Group and Southern Co-op receive final CMA approval
The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has given complete approval for the merger of the Co-op Group and Southern Co-op, marking a major milestone for the businesses.
This comes after a review from the watchdog this year, which raised concerns that the merger could reduce competition in certain local areas.
As part of the agreement made with the CMA, 15 convenience stores and two funeral homes would be divested as a solution for the concerns around competition.
Earlier this year a subsidiary of Co-op Group, Siena Co-operative Limited, acquired Southern Co-op and two businesses operated separately while awaiting the CMA’s approval.
The final approval now allows the two organisations to begin the process of merging the companies together and moving forward with integration plans.
The companies will now begin the merger process with the timing of transfers differing across various parts of the organisations.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
Both of the businesses will continue to operate independently and normally until detailed integration plans are finalised.
This marks a major move for the companies to create one of the biggest co-operative societies in the UK with over 300 years of operations.
Kate Allum, interim CEO of The Co-operative Group, said: “Today is a significant moment for our two societies and the wider co-operative movement. CMA approval gives us the green light to begin an exciting new chapter of co-operation.
“By bringing together more than 300 years of co-operative heritage, we have the opportunity to build an even stronger Co-op, with greater scale and resilience, and the ability to deliver more for our members, customers and communities.”
Southern Co-op currently operates 173 food stores and over 70 franchise locations, and Co-op Group has 2,300 food stores and a wholesale business.

items.title: N!CK’S expands UK supermarket presence with Morrisons, Sainsbury’s and Ocado listings
items.summary: Swedish snacking brand N!CK’S is ramping up its UK expansion with new listings across Morrisons, Sainsbury’s and Ocado as it looks to capitalise on growing demand for protein-rich snacks. The…
items.body:
N!CK’S expands UK supermarket presence with Morrisons, Sainsbury’s and Ocado listings
Swedish snacking brand N!CK’S is ramping up its UK expansion with new listings across Morrisons, Sainsbury’s and Ocado as it looks to capitalise on growing demand for protein-rich snacks.
The confectionery brand is expanding its grocery footprint alongside existing listings at Boots, as it looks to compete with traditional chocolate bars and established sports nutrition brands.
Its UK push centres on a range of protein wafer bars, which contain 10g of protein per 40g bar and no added sugar.
The range is available in five flavours, including Chocolate, Vanilla, Orange Chocolate, Hazelnut and Peanut Butter.
Alongside its supermarket expansion, N!CK’S is targeting the fitness market, with a rollout into PureGym planned for December.
The brand already has listings at Third Space, Bannatyne and Fitness First, as it looks to reach customers seeking convenient protein snacks beyond the traditional sports nutrition aisle.
Founded in Sweden in 2013 by Niclas Luthman, N!CK’S has expanded into 15 international markets, selling products across confectionery, protein bars, ice cream and sweeteners.
The business said its non-frozen sales grew 33 per cent between 2023 and 2025, driven by demand across its confectionery and protein bar ranges.
The latest UK listings come as more food and drink brands look to tap into the growing popularity of high-protein products, with supermarkets increasingly expanding their ranges to cater to health-conscious shoppers.
N!CK’S vice president of sales Jesper Mathiasson said: “The UK is a hugely exciting market for N!CK’S, and these new retail partnerships are a major step forward in our ambition to make better-for-you snacking more accessible.
“We believe people should never have to choose between a genuinely delicious treat and making more considered food choices.
“That’s why we put taste at the heart of everything we do, with no added sugar and protein adding to the appeal.”
The brand is positioning its wafer bars as an everyday alternative to traditional confectionery, betting that consumers will increasingly look for snacks that combine familiar flavours with additional nutritional benefits.

items.title: Russia denies involvement in cyberattacks on supermarket fridges across Europe
items.summary: Russia has denied involvement in a wave of cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe, which have forced retailers to throw away millions of pounds worth of fresh and frozen…
items.body:
Russia denies involvement in cyberattacks on supermarket fridges across Europe
Russia has denied involvement in a wave of cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe, which have forced retailers to throw away millions of pounds worth of fresh and frozen food.
The attacks saw hackers remotely access temperature controls at grocery stores, raising temperatures in fridges and freezers to as high as 55°C and causing widespread disruption.
Retailers across several European countries, including Belgium, Sweden, Ireland and France, have been affected, with some stores forced to remove chilled and frozen products from sale.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov dismissed allegations of Russian involvement as “absurd”, insisting there was no evidence linking Moscow to the incidents.
The denial comes after two pro-Russian hacking groups, NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance, claimed responsibility for the attacks in posts on Telegram, which were subsequently deleted.
However, cybersecurity experts have warned that the groups’ claims have not been independently verified, while authorities have yet to formally identify those responsible.
Among the retailers affected are Carrefour and Delhaize in Belgium, alongside Swedish supermarket chains Coop and ICA.
In Ireland, 13 SuperValu stores were impacted, forcing the removal of chilled and frozen products before the issue was resolved.
The attacks have also reached the UK, where three meat suppliers were targeted through vulnerabilities in their refrigeration control systems, although no stock losses were reported.
The latest incidents follow a similar cyberattack in France last month, when refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets were compromised, resulting in significant food losses.
Cybersecurity specialists believe attackers have been exploiting weaknesses in internet-connected refrigeration controllers, allowing them to manipulate temperatures remotely.
The incidents have raised concerns about the vulnerability of supermarket infrastructure, particularly as retailers increasingly rely on connected technology to monitor refrigeration and manage energy consumption.
US authorities have also warned of an ongoing threat to industrial refrigeration systems, urging businesses to strengthen cybersecurity measures, install software updates and restrict public internet access to temperature controls.
While Russia has rejected suggestions of its involvement, investigations into the attacks remain ongoing.

items.title: Howes Percival’s Katie James on why a turnaround may not be enough to save Poundland
items.summary: Poundland’s improving trading hasn’t kept it out of a fight over its future. Howes Percival partner Katie James explains why its lenders hold the cards, what administration would mean and how far the fallout could spread… Poundland’s predicament is hard to square. After a year of restructuring, the chain is showing signs of recovery. Yet...
items.body:
Poundland’s improving trading hasn’t kept it out of a fight over its future. Howes Percival partner Katie James explains why its lenders hold the cards, what administration would mean and how far the fallout could spread…
Poundland’s predicament is hard to square. After a year of restructuring, the chain is showing signs of recovery. Yet administration looms, with some 12,000 jobs at risk.
The problem, says Katie James, partner at law firm Howes Percival, is that a business can become healthier without becoming healthy enough for those financing it.
“Profit is great. It means you can pay your employees and your current debts,” she tells Retail Gazette. “But if it’s not making sufficient profit, it can’t eat into that debt.”
When Pepco sold Poundland to Gordon Brothers for £1 in 2025, restructuring was already part of the plan. Has it secured a future or merely bought time?
James points to the financing underpinning the deal, including a £95 million asset-based lending facility from Gordon Brothers and lending from former owner Pepco. The latest filed accounts do not reveal precisely how much remains outstanding.
“There has clearly been a lot of work done to restructure and get it into a profitable position on a day-to-day basis,” she says. “But it may not be quite enough to repay Pepco and Gordon Brothers as they want.”
The result is pressure between management and secured lenders.
“The directors are saying, ‘We’re going in the right direction; we want to do this.’ But the secured creditors are saying, ‘It’s not happening fast enough. We can see more problems on the horizon, and we want to make a change.’”
Why the lenders can act
Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, but administration has not yet begun. Nor must a qualifying secured lender necessarily wait for formal insolvency to intervene.
“When directors appoint administrators, the company needs to be insolvent,” she says. “When a secured lender appoints administrators, it doesn’t have to be formally insolvent. There can be a breach of the lending arrangements and a concern that its security is at risk.”
Administration is not, however, simply a mechanism for a shareholder to recover its investment.
“Administrators are officers of the court. They have a duty to act in the best interests of all creditors, not just the secured creditors.”
The legal objectives are to rescue the company, improve creditors’ return compared with liquidation, or realise assets for secured or preferential creditors where the other objectives cannot reasonably be achieved.
Poundland could trade while seeking a buyer, be sold immediately through a pre-pack administration, or be broken up.
James thinks the costs of trading through administration will loom large in any decision.
“If they’re trading the business, wages for employees still employed after 14 days become an expense of the administration,” she explains. “Administrators won’t want to trade without really good visibility on trading profits.”
Christmas stock may already be moving through warehouses, and time to secure a deal is limited.
“It’s still going to be relatively chaotic. It’s still going to be relatively fast-moving,” James says. “Some people can work with that; some people can’t.”
A rescue, and the limits of pressure
Potential buyers include Martin Property Group, while Poundland founder Steve Smith has discussed his interest. Interest, however, is not a deal.
James believes political and public scrutiny may have widened the rescue discussion.
“I don’t think anybody wants to see 12,000 redundancies in the lead-up to Christmas,” she says. She welcomes Gordon Brothers’ statement that it will consider solutions aimed at preserving jobs.
“Are there better ways of doing these things?” she asks. “Do they have to result in such an immediate response? Can we have a little bit longer? Can we wait for repayment a little longer?”
She cannot say whether a break-up was ever the intended outcome, selling assets separately can generate greater returns, but the public financial information is insufficient to draw that conclusion.
Multiple bidders could help.
“That increases competition, which increases value,” James says. “I don’t think the publicity has done any harm in generating interest to acquire the business as a going concern.”
Lenders control whether to appoint administrators; after appointment, decisions rest with the administrators.
Christmas stock and the supplier squeeze
James is particularly concerned about what would happen beyond Poundland’s own payroll.
“I’ve always likened business relationships to a spider’s web,” she says. “You’ve got the business, employees, landlords, customers and suppliers. All of those little webs are susceptible to insolvency, and the impact can be quite catastrophic.”
Christmas stock may already be manufactured, in transit or warehoused. Smaller suppliers could depend heavily on Poundland.
James has seen suppliers alter terms to limit exposure.
“Some are now saying, ‘We want cash on delivery.’ Nothing beats cash,” she says. Others may seek to reclaim goods under retention-of-title provisions if they have not been paid.
That could undermine plans to trade through Christmas.
“If they’ve got too many suppliers doing that, what are they going to have to sell in the lead-up to Christmas?”
James also recalls Woolworths’ disappearance. Other shops lost passing trade when shoppers lost a reason to visit.
“Poundland is a similar prospect,” she says. “You go to Poundland for something and pop into other shops. If you haven’t got those destination shops on the high street, why will people go?”
The warning signs, and a reason to fight
For those within the industry watching events unfold, James’s advice is to treat deteriorating communication as seriously as deteriorating finances.
“Silence is the biggest one,” she says. “If the finance director or directors of your customer aren’t returning your calls, something is going on.”
Late deliveries and unpaid invoices are other warnings. Long relationships can offer false reassurance.
“We all want to believe the best in people, especially when you’ve worked with somebody for 10 or 20 years. You think, ‘He’ll see me right.’ But sometimes the law says he can’t see you right,” she warns. “Early advice gives you options.”
For Poundland, consumer loyalty remains an asset, but familiarity isn’t enough.
“Retailers have to be very clear about their offering,” she says. “People want to know they can get something before they even go into the shop.”
Consumers and financial stakeholders both have a role, she argues.
“There’s no point going through what will be a very expensive process with something like Poundland if the consumers don’t return.”
The immediate legal question is whether a rescue can satisfy creditors. The longer commercial question is whether Poundland can give shoppers a compelling reason to come back. Neither can be answered by a short spell of improved trading alone.

items.title: M&S puts food at heart of 2026 Christmas advert starring James Norton
items.summary: Marks & Spencer has launched its 2026 Christmas advertising campaign, placing festive food and family celebrations at the centre of a cross-category push spanning its grocery, fashion, home and beauty…
items.body:
M&S puts food at heart of 2026 Christmas advert starring James Norton
Marks & Spencer has launched its 2026 Christmas advertising campaign, placing festive food and family celebrations at the centre of a cross-category push spanning its grocery, fashion, home and beauty businesses.
Titled The Home of Christmas, the campaign stars actor James Norton as an undercover Santa, alongside Lucy Punch as Mrs Claus, who persuades him to leave the North Pole and experience Christmas celebrations for himself.
The film follows Santa as he swaps his traditional red suit for a Christmas jumper and shaves off his beard to go unnoticed. His journey takes in festive meals, shopping for gifts and preparing the home for Christmas, highlighting the role of food in bringing families and friends together.
M&S research found that 68 per cent of its customers believe food is what makes Christmas feel special, while 81 per cent want to enjoy a special Christmas with the people they love.
The retailer also revealed that it sells nearly three mince pies every second during the festive period, while one in three Christmas turkeys sold in the UK comes from M&S.
Food featured in the campaign includes the Oakham Turkey Crown with Italian Chestnut, Pancetta and Calabrian Orange Stuffing, priced at £70.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
Andrew Hicks, food marketing director at M&S, said: “Christmas is made up of countless moments, traditions and rituals that mean something different to every family. For generations, M&S has been privileged to play a part in those celebrations, helping customers create a Christmas that feels uniquely their own.
“From the food shared around the table to the thoughtful finishing touches that make the season memorable, we’re proud to be part of some of the moments that matter most.”
The campaign marks the first time since 2017 that M&S has brought Food, Fashion, Home and Beauty together in one Christmas advertising campaign.
It will run across television, video-on-demand, cinema, outdoor advertising, social media, radio and digital channels. Customers will also be able to access festive recipes through the M&S Recipe Hub and check ingredient and product availability through its digital catalogue.
The film features a specially recorded version of Belinda Carlisle’s Heaven Is a Place on Earth, performed by Katherine Jenkins, who also makes an appearance in the advert.
The campaign launches on M&S’s Instagram and YouTube channels on 6 November, with its television debut during ITV’s This Morning.

items.summary: Seasalt Cornwall has unveiled its Christmas 2026 campaign, featuring an all-female Cornish sea shanty group. The campaign, filmed in Charlestown Harbour, centres on the theme of homecoming and features 15-piece group Femmes de la Mer performing ‘Cornwall My Home’ against the backdrop of a traditional lantern parade. The film features handmade paper lanterns created by...
items.body:
Seasalt Cornwall has unveiled its Christmas 2026 campaign, featuring an all-female Cornish sea shanty group.
The campaign, filmed in Charlestown Harbour, centres on the theme of homecoming and features 15-piece group Femmes de la Mer performing ‘Cornwall My Home’ against the backdrop of a traditional lantern parade.
The film features handmade paper lanterns created by local artist Imogen Bone, with the retailer drawing on its Cornish roots to tell a story of community, friendship and festive traditions.
It marks Seasalt’s third collaboration with the Falmouth-based group this year, following its spring/summer campaign featuring ‘Howlin Wind’ and autumn campaign featuring ‘Blood Red Roses’.
Seasalt has also sponsored a documentary about the group, Our Cornwall, produced by Grounded House Productions, which is set to be screened across the UK.
The Christmas film, created by Seasalt’s in-house team and led by creative director Katy Pople, will launch this weekend ahead of a wider advertising push throughout November and December.
For the first time, Seasalt will run its Christmas campaign across Channel 4, Netflix and Amazon Prime, using connected TV advertising formats that allow viewers to explore products worn by the performers from its festive collection.
The campaign will also appear across YouTube, print advertising and a digital partnership with The Telegraph, alongside imagery rolled out across Seasalt’s stores and online channels.
Seasalt currently operates 84 stores across the UK and Ireland, alongside its ecommerce business and wholesale partnerships with retailers including Marks & Spencer, Next, Nordstrom and Zalando.
The family-owned business, which was founded more than 40 years ago, has increasingly invested in brand storytelling and digital marketing as it looks to reach new customers beyond its traditional heartland.
