items.title: Waitrose commits to supplying British free range fresh turkeys
items.summary: Waitrose has announced a commitment to supply 100 per cent British, free-range fresh Christmas turkeys, marking a major move for animal welfare standards at the supermarket. This builds on a…
items.body:
Waitrose commits to supplying British free range fresh turkeys
Waitrose has announced a commitment to supply 100 per cent British, free-range fresh Christmas turkeys, marking a major move for animal welfare standards at the supermarket.
This builds on a long-standing partnership with Traditional Norfolk Poultry (TNP), which has a dedicated acreage made exclusively for Waitrose birds to move around freely.
Waitrose is launching two products as part of its premium No.1 range, which includes an exclusive rare heritage breed.
The supermarket retailer is stocking a British Free Range Bourbon Red Heritage Breed Turkey for a price of £110 for 5kg and the British Free Range Traditionally Prepared Bronze Turkey priced at £120 for 5kg.
Jake Pickering, head of agriculture at Waitrose said: “To be the first UK supermarket to guarantee that every single fresh Christmas turkey is 100 per cent British and free-range is a proud moment for us and sets a bold new welfare benchmark for the industry.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
“Animal welfare is at the very core of how we source, and by rearing our turkeys to the highest free-range standards with dedicated woodland and pasture to thrive in, we’re supporting local farmers while guaranteeing exceptional welfare and flavour.”
The move aims to respond to the shopper demand for sustainability, ethical farming, and high welfare practices.
This builds on the company’s ongoing efforts towards high animal welfare standards with a wide own-brand free-range selection, including eggs, milk, and cream.
Waitrose has introduced upgraded packaging that features ‘Free Range’ alongside animal welfare tiering to provide transparency for shoppers.
The supermarket retailer also anticipates high demand, with searches for ‘Christmas turkey’ surging by 1351 per cent in the last month on Waitrose.
The retailer’s fresh Christmas range is now available to pre-order online and in store from 19 December.

items.title: JD Sports rolls out stock-tracking technology across 414 stores to tackle availability and theft
items.summary: JD Sports has introduced RFID technology across 414 stores in the UK and Ireland to improve stock availability, speed up replenishment and tackle retail theft. The company recently partnered with Zebra Technologies to roll out the inventory-tracking system, which it says has helped achieve 98 per cent on-shelf availability and cut replenishment times by 20...
items.body:
JD Sports has introduced RFID technology across 414 stores in the UK and Ireland to improve stock availability, speed up replenishment and tackle retail theft.
The company recently partnered with Zebra Technologies to roll out the inventory-tracking system, which it says has helped achieve 98 per cent on-shelf availability and cut replenishment times by 20 per cent.
The tech allows store staff to scan products on the shop floor and in stockrooms without having to count each item individually, giving the retailer a more accurate picture of its inventory.
JD said the system has also helped staff move 95 per cent more stock from storerooms onto the shop floor, while reducing the time spent on manual stock checks.
The rollout followed a five-store trial and reached 414 UK and Ireland locations in around three months, with an average of 26 stores added each week.
It worked with technology suppliers Renovotec and Checkpoint Systems on the project, using the latter’s ItemOptix software to track inventory across its stores.
Alongside improving product availability, JD is using the technology to identify potential stock losses earlier, rather than relying on periodic audits that can take place months after an incident.
JD Sports head of customer operations Daniel McGrath said the technology had made it easier for store teams to manage stock without taking time away from customers.
The UK and Ireland deployment forms part of a wider international programme.
By September, JD had introduced RFID across 2,700 stores globally, including 1,000 directly operated locations, to improve inventory management across its business.

Sharry Cramond, fashion, home & beauty marketing director at M&S, said: “Customers don’t think about Christmas as one meal, one gift or one outfit. They think about all the moments that make the season special.

Bringing those categories together allows us to tell one connected Christmas story and celebrate all the ways our customers make the season their own. That’s why we’re proud that customers call M&S The Home of Christmas.”

Retailers across several European countries, including Belgium, Sweden, Ireland and France, have been affected, with some stores forced to remove chilled and frozen products from sale.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov dismissed allegations of Russian involvement as “absurd”, insisting there was no evidence linking Moscow to the incidents.
The denial comes after two pro-Russian hacking groups, NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance, claimed responsibility for the attacks in posts on Telegram, which were subsequently deleted.
However, cybersecurity experts have warned that the groups’ claims have not been independently verified, while authorities have yet to formally identify those responsible.
Among the retailers affected are Carrefour and Delhaize in Belgium, alongside Swedish supermarket chains Coop and ICA.
In Ireland, 13 SuperValu stores were impacted, forcing the removal of chilled and frozen products before the issue was resolved.
The attacks have also reached the UK, where three meat suppliers were targeted through vulnerabilities in their refrigeration control systems, although no stock losses were reported.
The latest incidents follow a similar cyberattack in France last month, when refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets were compromised, resulting in significant food losses.
Cybersecurity specialists believe attackers have been exploiting weaknesses in internet-connected refrigeration controllers, allowing them to manipulate temperatures remotely.
The incidents have raised concerns about the vulnerability of supermarket infrastructure, particularly as retailers increasingly rely on connected technology to monitor refrigeration and manage energy consumption.
US authorities have also warned of an ongoing threat to industrial refrigeration systems, urging businesses to strengthen cybersecurity measures, install software updates and restrict public internet access to temperature controls.
While Russia has rejected suggestions of its involvement, investigations into the attacks remain ongoing.

items.title: Marks & Spencer set for a very social and united Christmas as 2027 campaign kicks off today
items.summary: M&S is bringing fashion, home, beauty and food together in one Christmas campaign for the first time since 2017.The retailer's Home of Christmas offering launches on its Instagram page and YouTube channel at 7am today and stars James Norton as an undercover Santa, alongside Lucy Punch as Mr
items.body:
M&S is bringing fashion, home, beauty and food together in one Christmas campaign for the first time since 2017.
The retailer's Home of Christmas offering launches on its Instagram page and YouTube channel at 7am today and stars James Norton as an undercover Santa, alongside Lucy Punch as Mrs. Claus, with a special appearance and exclusive soundtrack by Katherine Jenkins.
Beyond the film, an integrated campaign will run across TV, video on demand, cinema, outdoor, social media, radio, digital display and print, alongside M&S’s owned channels, influencer activity and PR.
Across social and digital channels, the Friends of M&S will share their festive selections through M&S Love That Lists, featuring gifts, food, fashion, beauty and homeware. Customers will also be able to access festive recipes through a hub and check ingredient and product availability through a digital catalogue, supporting meal planning and shopping list preparation.
Sharry Cramond, Fashion, Home & Beauty Marketing Director at M&S, says: "Customers don't think about Christmas as one meal, one gift or one outfit. They think about all the moments that make the season special. As the only retailer with a truly cross-category offer spanning Food, Fashion, Beauty, Gifting and Home, M&S plays a unique role in helping customers create Christmas from start to finish. Bringing those categories together allows us to tell one connected Christmas story and celebrate all the ways our customers make the season their own. That's why we're proud that customers call M&S The Home of Christmas."
Andrew Hicks, Food Marketing Director at M&S, says: "Christmas is made up of countless moments, traditions and rituals that mean something different to every family. For generations, M&S has been privileged to play a part in those celebrations, helping customers create a Christmas that feels uniquely their own."
"From the food shared around the table to the thoughtful finishing touches that make the season memorable, we're proud to be part of some of the moments that matter most. This year's campaign brings that to life in a way that is warm, unexpected and full of charm, celebrating the special place M&S holds in our customers' festive traditions and reinforcing why we're proud to be The Home of Christmas."
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Social media was a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our winners were revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
The event consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.

items.title: M&S takes on John Lewis in Christmas ad battle with topless ‘shredded Santa’
items.summary: James Norton and Lucy Punch star as a youthful Mr and Mrs Claus in lively ad about shared moments as well as shopping For years the “Christmas advert moment” has belonged to one brand. John Lewis’s syrupy commercials featuring piano ballads and tearjerker storylines have given the 160-year-old department store a cultural head start in the dash for festive profits. This year, however, there’s one high-street rival with a sackful of tricks to make up the ground. Marks & Spencer has brought out the big guns – in the form of a topless Santa, played by the small-screen heart-throb James Norton . Continue reading...
items.body:
For years the “Christmas advert moment” has belonged to one brand. John Lewis’s syrupy commercials featuring piano ballads and tearjerker storylines have given the 160-year-old department store a cultural head start in the dash for festive profits.
This year, however, there’s one high-street rival with a sackful of tricks to make up the ground. Marks & Spencer has brought out the big guns – in the form of a topless Santa, played by the small-screen heart-throb James Norton.
The lively M&S Christmas ad has already drawn comparisons with John Lewis’s effort, which features Kristin Scott Thomas as a glamorous granny on the hunt to turn one room of her huge townhouse into a fun “gran cave”.
In the M&S corner Norton and Lucy Punch play a youthful Mr and Mrs Claus – with a lingering shot of Norton with his top off.
When John Lewis launched its advert this week, its portrayal of wealth was criticised, with a sprawling house and ungrateful grandchildren said to be out of touch with the wider mood of the nation.
But shots of Norton topless aside from an M&S white cotton towel have gone viral. Men’s Health magazine described him as a “shredded Santa”, saying his Saint Nick “leaves the traditional mince-pie physique looking a little dated”.
Gurjit Degun, the creativity and cultural editor at Campaign, a business magazine that covers advertising and marketing, described the M&S ad as “playful and tongue in cheek without being silly”.
M&S has combined its fashion, food, beauty and homeware strands into one campaign rather than individual adverts, a strategy it last used in 2017. Norton plays an undercover Santa who shaves off his beard so he can experience the buildup to Christmas incognito, while Punch is a snobbish Mrs Claus, similar to her character in Amandaland.
After the couple gatecrash a dinner party, swing by a children’s carol service and discover “picky bits”, the key takeaway from M&S is that Christmas is about shared moments rather than just big gifts. Although of course the advert is very much about shopping. Every element of it – from Punch’s pyjamas to that towel and the prawn cones Norton said he saw “hundreds” of during filming – is available to buy. Meanwhile, the main message derived from the John Lewis campaign is to give physical gifts rather than cold, hard cash.
Norton said the combination of a “playful, funny and reverent script” appealed to him. He is a “huge fan” of the advert’s director, Shannon Murphy, who has worked on shows including Killing Eve and Babyteeth.
“I trusted that Shannon would deliver on the tone,” he said. “She’s such a cool cat.” While he is usually “a sucker for a traditional tearjerker”, he believes the ad still captures the emotion of Christmas thanks to those family-and-friends moments that speak to “connection and joy”.
Punch said she liked the deliberately humorous script. “I don’t want any more Christmas tearjerkers,” she said. “I want fun and joy. Life is enough of a tearjerker, it’s fun to have something festive with a bit of a wink.”
In a tough consumer market, there is a lot weighing on the adverts’ success for the retailers. M&S is still trying to bounce back from a 2025 cyber hack that forced it to close its website for more than six weeks, costing it over £100m; John Lewis is trying to revive interest as it grapples with higher costs alongside a decline in consumer confidence.
Jonathan De Mello, the founder of JDM Retail consulting, describes the John Lewis strategy as smart, explaining that the casting of Scott Thomas reflected the type of customer the retailer was trying to appeal to.
“They are targeting a group that is fairly affluent,” he said. “They have a decent chunk of disposable income because they have paid off their mortgages.” However, this approach could “alienate the mass market”, he cautioned, as for a younger generation “it portrays a type of lifestyle that for many is unattainable”.
The M&S advert is a reflection of how the retailer has successfully turned its business around, De Mello said. “Before, there was a dichotomy between the food and the fashion, and now they are very much aligned. M&S now taps into the younger consumer psyche and this advert reflects this.”

items.title: Morrisons and Duvo connect as JD Sports reaps RFID rewards: this week's biggest retail technology stories
items.summary: It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Walmart and Symbotic, M&S, Vusion, Screwfix, Gophr, VoCoVo, Barron McCann, and the 2
items.body:
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Walmart and Symbotic, M&S, Vusion, Screwfix, Gophr, VoCoVo, Barron McCann, and the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
1. Walmart and Symbotic ramp up automation and AI powered supply chain transformation push
Symbotic and Walmart have announced an expanded tie up to bring automation capabilities to 25 US regional distribution centres, while supporting additional opportunities across the retail giant's global supply chain network.
The agreement includes an initial commitment of approximately $6 billion in spend, covering work over several years.
“Our partnership with Walmart started with a single product over a decade ago, and now we offer a full end-to-end solution to help power Walmart’s growth across its supply chain for years to come,” says Rick Cohen, Chairman and CEO at Symbotic. “This expanded agreement reflects the strength of that collaboration - a partnership defined by trust and shared ambition.”
2. Gophr powered Screwfix Sprint on demand delivery service now available in 600 stores
Screwfix Convenience is designed to drive usage of Screwfix Sprint delivery, Click & Collect and check-In services among tradespeople and DIY customers.
And the Sprint service, which promises delivery within 60 minutes, is now live at 600 stores and counting.
In a LinkedIn post, Max Britten, Managing Director UK & Ireland at Screwfix, said: "We know how important convenience is for our busy trade customers. They want to stay on the job, avoid unnecessary downtime and get what they need, when they need it. Sprint helps them do exactly that, with tens of thousands of customers using it so far this year."
He added: "So making Sprint accessible to more customers is a real priority for Screwfix. With the additional stores, it now reaches more than 62% of the UK population. A huge thank you to all our colleagues and our delivery partner Gophr who have helped us reach this important milestone, and of course to our customers for continuing to use Sprint."
3. Morrisons, Waitrose, and Dunelm take top honours at 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony in London
Focal Systems, PMC, Poq, VoCoVo, Deliverect, Enactor, SOLUM, Pricer, TCS, Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions, Vusion, Quorso, Datitude, and Sitoo were among the winners on Wednesday night at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
We received a record number of entries this year, showcasing truly impressive innovation across both traditional and digital retail spaces.
To quote a member of our star studded judging panel: "Reviewing such inventive, high impact solutions has been a truly rewarding experience. The depth of engineering, scalable architecture, and strategic vision displayed throughout the submissions underscores the rapid transformation happening across modern retail technology."
Our 2026 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC in Central London and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by actor, comedian and writer Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Congratulations to our 2026 winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Aurie Styla, and all those who attended last night’s gathering.
4. Retention.com CEO and Co-founder Adam Robinson, wife, and children among victims in Florida plane crash
A Learjet 60 was bound for the Bahamas from Austin when it nosedived into a multi-lane highway on 1st November. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating whether ice and turbulence contributed to the crash, and whether human error played a role.
E-commerce technology startup Retention.com CEO and Co-founder, Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp and their two children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were all killed in the crash.
A company spokesperson said: "We are heartbroken by the loss of Adam, his wife Helen and their two young children. Adam was much more than our CEO. He was a friend, a mentor and a bold, outspoken leader who lived life to the fullest. He cared deeply about the people around him and brought energy and conviction to everything he built. His loss is deeply felt across our team and the tech community, as we collectively mourn this significant loss."
They continued: "Our hearts are with Adam and Helen’s family and loved ones, and with everyone affected by the crash. We ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time. Our immediate focus at Retention.com is supporting our employees and Adam and Helen’s family. We are grateful for the kindness and support extended to them and our team."
5. Ahold Delhaize USA ramps up in-store technology modernisation push with NCR Voyix
Ahold Delhaize USA is expanding its work with NCR Voyix as it looks to modernise key in-store capabilities across Point of Sale, self-checkout, pharmacy and fuel operations.
The multi-year roll-out is now underway, with new PoS technology now available in 100 stores and additional deployment planned over the next several years.
“As we advance our technology strategy, we’re focused on making it easier for customers to shop with our brands and easier for our brands’ associates to serve their customers,” says Ann Dozier, Chief Information Officer at Ahold Delhaize USA.
“Our goal is to create a more consistent technology foundation and a more connected experience, while maintaining the flexibility that allows each of our local brands to meet its customers’ needs in the short-term and positions us for the future. The roll-out is underway with new PoS technology now available in 100 stores, with the roll-out continuing over the next several years.”
The selection of the Voyix Commerce Platform builds on Ahold Delhaize USA’s relationship with NCR Voyix, whose technology has supported the company’s operations for a number of years.
6. Retail technology specialist Barron McCann appoints Ian Thomas as Chief Executive Officer
Barron McCann has announced the appointment of Ian Thomas as Chief Executive Officer. He was previously at Node4 where he served as Chief Operating Officer.
Scott Watson, Co-owner at Barron McCann Group, says: "I have great pleasure in announcing the appointment of Ian Thomas to the role of Chief Executive Officer of Barron McCann, marking another exciting milestone in our continued growth journey. Ian brings a wealth of experience from an impressive career leading technology services organisations through periods of growth, transformation and operational excellence."
"Building on the already excellent reputation of Barron McCann’s service delivery, Ian will lead the continued scaling of the business in line with our ambitious growth targets. In addition to the Barron McCann CEO role, Ian will join our group board, helping to shape our wider group strategy and deliver operational synergies across our companies."
He adds: "One of the greatest strengths of being a family owned business is our ability to think beyond the short-term. We can invest with confidence, make decisions based on what is right for the future of our people and our businesses, and remain true to the values that have shaped the group from the very beginning. Ian’s appointment is another investment in our future."
"Just as importantly, his character and approach align naturally with our family culture and the way we do business. I’m confident he will be a great addition to the group, and I’m excited about what this next chapter will bring as we continue to create new opportunities and build on our success together."
7. VoCoVo hires former Waterstones exec Emma Hillyard as CFO and former CBRE technology chief Paul Birkin as CTO
Retail communications specialist, VoCoVo, has announced the appointments of Emma Hillyard as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Paul Birkin as Chief Technology Officer (CTO).
Hillyard has worked across both the private and not for profit sectors, including retail, with previous CFO roles at Waterstones, Blackwells and Alzheimer’s Society.
She says: “VoCoVo has achieved strong growth already, and my role is to help make sure we navigate this next period and build on the growth already seen. For me, that means giving teams the insight and support they need to make informed decisions and creating the right environment for people to do their best work."
"I’ve always been very people centric and believe culture is critical to making meaningful change stick. That was a big part of what attracted me to VoCoVo. Its people and culture are a real superpower, and I’m excited to build on that.”
Birkin has held C-suite positions at CBRE, Experian, Capita, Logica and Cisco.
He says, “I’ve spent much of my career leading large scale transformations where technology can make a visible difference. That’s what makes VoCoVo so exciting - there’s already a strong technology foundation and a true ambition to keep innovating. As retail becomes increasingly intelligent, AI has the potential to create huge business value. My focus is on turning that potential into tangible value for our customers and pushing what the connected store can deliver.”
8. JD Sports rolls out Zebra Technologies RFID tech across 414 stores in UK and Ireland
Zebra Technologies says that it has helped JD Sports to achieve 98% on-shelf availability and 20% faster replenishment, so high demand sizes move from the storeroom to the shelf when and where customers want them.
JD Sports has nearly 5,000 stores across 46 countries. As the retailer scaled, inventory visibility in stores remained a challenge. To reliably offer one-hour Click & Collect or 30-minute delivery, the stock count needed to be accurate. It sought a real-time inventory visibility solution that could support omnichannel retail, was easy for retail assistants to use and fast to roll-out across stores.
A pilot across five stores highlighted the capabilities of Zebra’s TC2 Series mobile computers paired with RFD40 UHF RFID sleds to read tags faster and at greater range. JD Sports also selected Zebra OneCare which allows its store associates to address everyday wear and tear and accidental damage by simply swapping devices at no cost if something breaks.
Alongside Zebra, JD Sports worked with Renovotec, a Zebra partner who led the device deployment, and Checkpoint Systems, a Zebra eegistered ISV who integrated its ItemOptix software, giving a single view of inventory data across the retailer.
"What Zebra gives us is the ability to scale with trust,” says Daniel McGrath, Head of Customer Operations, JD Sports. “Things just land and work. Colleagues open a box, turn it on, and they are up and running. That lets our teams spend their time where it matters: with the customer.”
9. Morrisons partners with Duvo as UK grocery giant eyes opportunities for AI adoption
Morrisons has partnered with Duvo.ai as it looks to identify opportunities to make greater use of AI across its existing systems.
Duvo was co-founded by Tomáš Čupr, who founded Rohlik Group, the European online grocer. It identifies and automates repetitive business tasks, freeing up team members to focus on decision-making, creativity, customer service and partner relationships.
The project will start by capturing how processes actually work across the UK grocery retailer's people, teams and systems. Duvo will then help it identify opportunities to simplify and redesign those processes, focusing where AI can create the most value, and highlighting a pathway for their swift adoption into everyday operations.
"Our business processes have evolved over decades and Duvo gives us a way to understand them in detail, and quickly," says Gordon MacPherson, Group Productivity Director at Morrisons.
"It means decisions about which repetitive everyday tasks to simplify, redesign and automate can be based on evidence rather than assumptions. That will give us a much clearer path from identifying AI opportunities to putting them into operation, freeing up our people to concentrate on high value work for the benefit of colleagues and customers."
10. Marks and Spencer taps Vusion EdgeSense platform amid retailer's store modernisation push
Vusion reports that Marks & Spencer will deploy its Connected Store platform to a number of new stores, with further roll-out potential in the future.
The deployment will support the retailer's focus on modernising store operations and improving the in-store experience for customers and colleagues.
Built on Bluetooth enabled infrastructure, Vusion's EdgeSense platform is designed to help connect store systems, product information and colleague activity more effectively across the shopfloor.
The initial deployment will focus on practical operational improvements, including managing product information more effectively, supporting colleagues in locating products more efficiently through location aware capabilities such as flashing labels, helping simplify in-store inventory processes and shopfloor execution, and creating a digital foundation that may support further store innovation over time.
Roy Horgan, CEO UK & Ireland at Vusion, says: “We are pleased to be working with M&S as it continues to invest in its store estate and colleague experience. Our Connected Store platform is designed to help retailers improve operational execution while providing the infrastructure to support future innovation.”

items.body:
Mamas & Papas has announced the appointment of Helen Monks as Group Brand & Marketing Director and Jessica Hodgson as Chief Financial Officer.
Monks joins following a career within the Regatta Group, where she most recently held the position of Brand & Marketing Director. During her time with the business, she led marketing activity across Regatta, Dare 2b and Regatta Professional, spanning brand strategy, campaigns, digital marketing, retail and product.
She says: "Mamas & Papas is a brand people have a real connection with, and I loved the idea of being part of what comes next. I'm looking forward to getting to know the team and helping the brand feel even more relevant to today's parents. As a mum myself, it's a world I care about personally too."
Hodgson brings ten years at KPMG working in corporate and project finance. She has also served as Retail Finance & Group Data Director at Pets at Home, and held senior finance, transformation and commercial leadership roles at Amazon, Morrisons and Asda.
Sarah Ashby, COO, says: "We’re delighted to welcome Helen and Jessica to Mamas & Papas at such an exciting point in our journey. Both bring exceptional experience, strong leadership and fresh thinking that will strengthen our team as we accelerate our growth ambitions in the UK and internationally. With an exciting 2027 and beyond ahead, their appointments add further strength and capability as we build the next chapter of Mamas & Papas and realise the significant opportunity ahead of us.”

Retail Technology Innovation of the Week is a series brought to you by RTIH, highlighting stand out deployments, launches, and initiatives by retailers and tech suppliers.
Every week, we showcase forward thinking tech plays that have impressed our Editor and the Retail Technology Innovations Report judging panel, building up to the publication of the 2026 report later this year.
And this week we’re focusing on Morrisons which has partnered with Duvo.ai as it looks to identify opportunities to make greater use of AI across its existing systems.

"It means decisions about which repetitive everyday tasks to simplify, redesign and automate can be based on evidence rather than assumptions. That will give us a much clearer path from identifying AI opportunities to putting them into operation, freeing up our people to concentrate on high value work for the benefit of colleagues and customers."
And honourable mentions this week to...
M&S
Vusion reports that Marks & Spencer will deploy its Connected Store platform to a number of new stores, with further roll-out potential in the future.
The deployment will support the retailer's focus on modernising store operations and improving the in-store experience for customers and colleagues.

Our Connected Store platform is designed to help retailers improve operational execution while providing the infrastructure to support future innovation.”
Seed to Table
Seed to Table, a grocery retailer in Naples, Florida, has created Goldie, a conversational AI avatar who shoppers can talk to via a full size Proto Hologram screen.
“Seed To Table is a cutting-edge grocery store/entertainment Mecca like no other and adding Goldie to it just brings us to another level that no other supermarket has,” says Dan St. Martin, General Manager. "We are the Disney World of supermarkets.”
At the entrance, a seven-foot Proto Hologram presents information, advertising and Goldie, which has a face, voice and whimsical personality. Shoppers can ask Goldie questions, get recommendations and discover ideas. She can also remember preferences and previous interactions.
Throughout the store, participating brands use QR enabled shelf displays. Shoppers can scan to discover a brand story, learn about a product, receive an offer or recommendation, and explore content created specifically around what they’re seeing.
“Seed to Table deserves tremendous credit for having the vision to be first,” says James Beckmann, CEO at Live Buzz Intelligence. “They’re showing what is possible when a retailer modernises engagement at exactly the right moment. We’re excited to bring something genuinely new to shoppers.”

JD Sports also selected Zebra OneCare which allows its store associates to address everyday wear and tear and accidental damage by simply swapping devices at no cost if something breaks.
Alongside Zebra, JD Sports worked with Renovotec, a Zebra partner who led the device deployment, and Checkpoint Systems, a Zebra eegistered ISV who integrated its ItemOptix software, giving a single view of inventory data across the retailer.
"What Zebra gives us is the ability to scale with trust,” says Daniel McGrath, Head of Customer Operations, JD Sports. “Things just land and work. Colleagues open a box, turn it on, and they are up and running. That lets our teams spend their time where it matters: with the customer.”
£28.52 billion...British consumers will splash out a record £28.52 billion online between 1st November and 31st December 2026, according to research released by Adobe.
Spending this year is anticipated to increase by 6.2% year-on-year (YoY) as total Q4 (October–December) e-commerce spend is projected to reach £40 billion (+6.4% YoY). Powered by Adobe Analytics, the research analyses direct consumer transactions across hundreds of billions of visits to UK retailer websites, tracking 100 million SKUs across 18 product categories.
The findings reveal a consumer base that is spending with greater intent, leveraging deep online price advantages, relying on social and influencer discovery, and increasingly turning to generative AI assistants to uncover the best value.
8...Focal Systems, PMC, Poq, VoCoVo, Deliverect, Enactor, SOLUM, Pricer, TCS, Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions, Vusion, Quorso, Datitude, and Sitoo were among the winners on Wednesday night at the eighth edition of the RTIH Innovation Awards.
We received a record number of entries this year, showcasing truly impressive innovation across both traditional and digital retail spaces.
To quote a member of our star studded judging panel: "Reviewing such inventive, high impact solutions has been a truly rewarding experience. The depth of engineering, scalable architecture, and strategic vision displayed throughout the submissions underscores the rapid transformation happening across modern retail technology."
Our 2026 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC in Central London and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by actor, comedian and writer Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Congratulations to our 2026 winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Aurie Styla, and all those who attended last night’s gathering.
236 MediaMarktSaturn stores across 141 cities in Germany are now available on Just Eat's Lieferando Deutschland service.
In a LinkedIn post, the retailer said: "Someone in Berlin once ordered over 7,200 euros worth of laptops and smartphones through a food delivery app. It arrived within the hour. That's the extreme end of what's now possible through our expanded partnership with Lieferando Deutschland. Most orders are a lot smaller, a power bank, a missing cable, a couple of AirTags, but the range stretches from one end to the other."
The rapid delivery service is growing from ten cities to 141 across Germany. The product range is also expanding, up to 10,000 items per store, delivered within an hour, Monday to Saturday, at the same prices as in stores.
One and three...TSB is warning online shoppers to be on their guard against widespread purchase fraud ahead of Black Friday and Christmas, as new research (involving 2,000 Brits) reveals one in three has fallen victim to a purchase scam on social media or secondhand platforms.
TSB's own internal data found that purchase fraud accounts for 45% of all TSB bank transfer losses, and up by 4% year-on-year. Younger shoppers are most likely to have experienced this, with 49% of 25–34-year-olds and 44% of 18–24-year-olds having been caught out. Overall, 53% of Brits surveyed have either fallen victim to purchase fraud themselves or know someone who has, highlighting the scale of the issue.
With Black Friday and Christmas approaching, polling shows that consumers expect to spend an average of £245 on gifts and purchases over this period. TSB is urging consumers to be vigilant, with customer data showing that purchase fraud losses total £2.3million at TSB this year alone and with an average loss of £540 per customer.
Its customer data also reveals that Facebook accounts for two thirds of cases (65%), followed by TikTok (14%), Snapchat (7%) and Instagram (6%).
100...Two independent convenience retailers say their Just Eat business has grown around fivefold since they stopped updating marketplace listings by hand, as the number of indies using Snappy Technologies’ Order Aggregation (OA) platform passes 100.
OA brings orders from Just Eat, Uber Eats, Deliveroo, Foodhub and Snappy Shopper onto one device and sends price, promotion and stock changes to every platform at once.
Independent users trade under fascias including Premier, Morrisons Daily, Keystore, Costcutter, Nisa and Londis. Across independents and retail groups, including East of England Co-op and Southern Co-op, OA has now processed more than half a million orders, with over 300 stores currently trading on the platform.
6 and 75...AI assistants are becoming the place shoppers ask what to buy, and the next step, letting an AI agent buy for you, is already live for US shoppers in Gemini, Meta's Muse and Microsoft Copilot.
Research published by Human Forward, a startup based out of London, shows most of Britain's best known brands are not ready for this brave new world.
Human Forward asked six AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google's Gemini, DeepSeek and Meta's Muse) the questions shoppers ask about 75 leading UK retailers and direct to consumer brands, and checked each brand's website for the standards AI agents use to find products and complete a purchase. It found:
Most brands can't be bought by an AI agent. Of the 50 sites it could check, 35 were not set up for an AI agent to buy from, including Marks and Spencer, Dunelm and Moonpig. The 15 that were ready all run on Shopify, which builds it in for its merchants. Brands on their own technology have been left to work it out alone.
One in five is never recommended. Asked for the best brands in their own category, no assistant named 15 of the 75 brands. Among the big retailers it was 12 of 50, including boohoo, New Look, Matalan, River Island, Schuh and AO.
The assistants disagree. When one assistant recommends a brand, on average 39% of the others leave it out. ChatGPT is the hardest to get into: it named a brand unprompted 40% of the time, against 60% for Claude.
Everyday names get lost. Ask an assistant “What is Iceland?” and all six describe the country, not the supermarket.
Being recommended is not being ready. Moonpig tops the table for AI answers at 99 out of 100, yet no agent checkout was found on its site.
26...Currys opened its new Cambridge store last Friday. The retailer has relocated to new premises a few doors along from its previous store at Cambridge Retail Park, marking its 26th year in the city.
New digital screens, an upgraded gaming zone, hands on demo areas and a Business Hub aim to put customers at the heart of the design, giving them more ways to see, feel and try tech.
“I’m so excited about the opening, and about where it takes Currys next, with our stores and online working together as one," says Lindsay Haselhurst, Chief Operating Officer at Currys.
"Colleagues are at the very heart of what makes us special, and our stores give them a brilliant place to bring amazing technology to life, helping customers discover, experience and get the most from the latest tech. I can’t wait to welcome Cambridge customers into the new store and see them enjoying even more ways to see, feel and try the tech for themselves."
The store will also test improvements that could be introduced elsewhere across the retailer's almost 300 locations estate, depending on customer response and results.
One in nine self-checkouts in London convenience stores are out of action at any given moment because of technical faults, according to new research released by Scalefusion.
The research, covering 730 self-checkouts in 100 London stores run by four of the UK’s largest supermarket brands, found that on average 11% of machines were unavailable to shoppers. In one instance, every self-checkout was running but none could take contactless card payments, a fault that lasted for several days in a row.
Scalefusion is warning that, with so many convenience stores competing for the same customers, a single faulty machine will create delays and queues that erode customer experience and drive business elsewhere.
The Virgin Media O2 Business Movers Index found that 38% of UK shoppers have left a store or avoided returning because of complicated or unreliable technology, rising to 51% among Gen Z. Self-checkouts top the list of frustrations, cited by 33%.
74%, 73% and 61%...Research published by the Coalition for Trusted Reviews (CfTR), an alliance bringing together Amazon, Booking.com, Expedia Group, G2, Holidaycheck, Tripadvisor and Trustpilot, has revealed growing concerns around fake reviews and how they affect purchasing decisions.
The research is based on a survey of 6,000 people across the UK, Italy, and the US. While eight in ten consumers in the UK (85%), US (82%), and Italy (80%) use online reviews at least sometimes when considering a purchase, 74% of UK consumers, 73% of Americans and 61% of Italians have decided not to purchase a product or service due to concerns about fake or misleading reviews.
Although many online platforms invest heavily in fighting misuse, review fraud is becoming increasingly sophisticated. Bad actors - those who attempt to breach platform guidelines and mislead consumers and businesses via fake reviews - operate across platforms and jurisdictions, reusing identities, tactics and networks. This makes it challenging for any single platform or regulator to disrupt fraudulent activity.
Review and user verification is one of several methods online platforms may use to combat fake content. However, the research also highlights a tension between consumers' desire for authentic reviews and their willingness to accept additional verification measures. In the UK, 56% of consumers say that being required to provide ID would make them less likely to leave a review, alongside 46% in the US and 43% in Italy.
$1.5 billion and $21.5 billion...Zipline has announced a $1.5 billion raise at a $21.5 billion post-money valuation, led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest, and Salesforce Ventures.
It will use the capital to expand its US manufacturing facilities and ramp up hiring as it builds a drone delivery network across the country.
Walmart and Zipline are working together to launch 300 additional sites as part of a new national multi-year agreement with potential to grow further. Uber is targeting one million deliveries a day with Zipline by 2029.
“Zipline is now one of the largest autonomous robotics companies in the world - operating with scale, safety, and a magical user experience for consumers and merchants,” says Matt Huang, Co-Founder and Managing Partner at Paradigm. “It's no wonder that some of the largest merchants in the world are partnering with Zipline to use their delivery network.”
Screwfix Convenience is designed to drive usage of Screwfix Sprint delivery, Click & Collect and check-In services among tradespeople and DIY customers.
And the Sprint service, which promises delivery within 60 minutes, is now live at 600 stores and counting.
In a LinkedIn post, Max Britten, Managing Director UK & Ireland at Screwfix, said: "We know how important convenience is for our busy trade customers. They want to stay on the job, avoid unnecessary downtime and get what they need, when they need it. Sprint helps them do exactly that, with tens of thousands of customers using it so far this year."
He added: "So making Sprint accessible to more customers is a real priority for Screwfix. With the additional stores, it now reaches more than 62% of the UK population. A huge thank you to all our colleagues and our delivery partner Gophr who have helped us reach this important milestone, and of course to our customers for continuing to use Sprint."
26...Just Eat has announced a new partnership with Lindt & Sprungli UK to bring its chocolate range straight to customers’ doors in as little as 30 minutes. This makes it the brand's first delivery aggregator partner.
Customers can now order various Lindt's products from 26 locations across the UK. The brand's Pick & Mix offering is available with over 25 flavours available, including exclusives only sold from Lindt stores & Lindor flavours such as Shortbread, Pistachio, and Cherry Blossom Sakura.
From early next year, customers in eight locations will also gain exclusive delivery access to the Lindt Chocolate Bar through the Just Eat app, offering ‘Crema Gelata’ ice cream, hot chocolates and coffees.
A Just Eat spokesperson said: "The partnership marks another step in expanding our gifting offer ahead of the festive season, so as we approach Christmas there’s no need to worry about securing those last minute presents."

items.title: Bank's rate hike madness puts a choke hold on growth and will bring hardship to thousands, warns MAGGIE PAGANO
items.summary: High Street giant Next warns that shoppers are cutting their spending ahead of Christmas as the squeeze on households gets ever tighter.
items.body:
Bank's rate hike madness puts a choke hold on growth and will bring hardship to thousands, warns MAGGIE PAGANO
So what possessed the Bank of England to raise interest rates?
Already high street giant Next warns that shoppers are cutting their spending ahead of Christmas as the squeeze on household budgets gets ever tighter.
Meanwhile BT is to axe thousands more jobs, having slashed more than 11,000 jobs already this year.
Housebuilder Vistry is closing half of its regional operations and sacking staff to reduce its mounting debt pile in the face of falling demand for its homes, often social or affordable housing.
Vistry’s warning follows on from news this week that Britain’s biggest brick maker, Ibstock, has slashed brick making by a fifth due to collapsing demand.
These are hardly the signs of an overheating economy, let alone a healthy one.
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned there may be more interest rate rises to come if the Middle East conflict continues
Yet the Bank of England in its wisdom – some would say madness – took a hawkish stance by increasing interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point to 4 per cent, the first rise in more than three years.
All nine members of the Monetary Policy Committee agreed on a rise, with one voting for a half percentage point increase.
What’s more, Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, warns of more rises to come if the Middle East conflict continues, pushing energy and fuel costs even higher.
The more extreme hawks are suggesting that if there is no resolution to the war between the US and Iran, rates could go up again as soon as next month or early next year.
Why, then, have the Bank’s policy makers decided to make borrowing and mortgages more expensive for small businesses and householders at a time when the cost of living is so very costly?
The Bank’s position also sits oddly with more pessimistic forecasts for next year’s growth presented by the Office for Budget Responsibility last week.
More worryingly, the Treasury’s main independent forecaster reckons the economy will grow by just 1 per cent next year, with consumer prices peaking at 3.75 per cent compared with the Bank’s own growth and inflation figures, respectively at 1.6 per cent and 4.9 per cent.
Even though oil prices are down significantly since President Trump’s historic defeat in the midterm elections, Bailey says there are still inflationary pressures in the pipeline.
Adding fuel to the fire, household energy costs are set to rise again in January when Ofgem lifts electricity prices by up to another 27 per cent.
Peel Hunt’s economist Kallum Pickering says the Bank has acted ‘ahead of the evidence, not on it’ with ‘limited evidence of knock-on effects’ of higher energy prices.
It certainly has. If you want to be kind, you could say the Bank is still suffering from the loss of credibility suffered after the Covid crisis, when it was too slow to put up rates, calling inflation ‘transitory’.
But doing so now is counter-productive as it only serves to weaken demand, bringing hardship to thousands. More pertinently, higher rates cannot stop an external supply shock such as higher oil prices brought about by war in the Middle East.
What’s for sure is that thousands of small businesses and households have more to suffer.
According to Moneyfacts, the average two-year fixed-rate mortgage deal is now 5.97 per cent, up from 4.83 per cent at the start of the year.
On average, annual mortgage costs have risen by more than £2,000 since Trump’s first strikes on Iran.
But there is a silver lining. Nearly nine out of ten of all home mortgages are on fixed-rate deals. Most of these have risen sharply over the past year because of the forecasts of higher rates to come.
As these increases are now baked in, it’s entirely possible that the cost of some fixed-rate offers could fall despite the rise in base rate. With 2.3m mortgages due to expire next year, that would be good news.
A toast to spirited leadership
There was a nice bounce to Diageo yesterday after excellent first-quarter trading, taking shares to an eight-month high.
Ex-Tesco boss Dave Lewis is coming up to his first year running Diageo and is clearly having a ball.
Although the shares are still half of what they were five years ago, they have performed strongly this year as Lewis set about cost-cutting and streamlining the drinks giant.
There’s been a big emphasis on marketing, no doubt helped by being one of the World Cup sponsors. Guinness – the powerhouse of Diageo – is storming ahead, with double-digit growth around the world.
There’s just one problem: summer heatwaves saw sales dip in the UK. Lewis says Diageo is working on a solution. Whatever is he cooking up? A new brew?

items.body:
MINISO UK will open the UK’s first MINISO FRIENDS store at St David’s Cardiff in 2027, more than doubling its footprint in the centre and introducing its larger-format, IP-led concept to the UK market.
| FORMAT | MINISO FRIENDS – larger-format, IP-led concept store | 
| LOCATION | St David’s Cardiff, close to M&S, Primark and Boots | 
| SIZE | 6,600+ sq ft (from 2,637 sq ft) · 35m+ frontage | 
| OPENING | 2027 | 
| SIGNIFICANCE | First MINISO FRIENDS in the UK and Wales | 
MINISO FRIENDS combines retail, experience and community, with dedicated IP toy zones, an extensive collectables range including blind boxes, plush and licensed merchandise, and MINISO’s full lifestyle, home, stationery, gifting and accessories offer. The format is designed to turn a shopping trip into a destination visit, increasing dwell time and giving fans and collectors a reason to travel.
The move builds on MINISO’s presence at St David’s since November 2020, when Cardiff became its second UK store and first outside London.
“MINISO FRIENDS is our most immersive format, and St David’s is the right place to bring it to the UK first. Cardiff has been a strong store for us since 2020, and this move more than doubles our space in a centre that continues to attract the best names in retail and leisure. The format is built around IP, collectables and experience – the things that turn a visit into a destination – and it sets the standard for how we want customers to experience MINISO across the UK.”
Saad Usman, COO, MINISO UK
Pablo Sueiras, Head of Retail & Hospitality Leasing at Landsec, said: “MINISO’s decision to more than double its footprint and select St David’s for the UK debut of MINISO Friends reflects the strength of the destination and the opportunity we see in Cardiff.
“We’re seeing significant growth in collectables, with collaborations around globally recognised IP helping MINISO build a highly engaged community. MINISO Friends takes that a step further, creating a bigger, more immersive format where those fans can come together around the characters they love.
“MINISO Friends will bring something completely new to Cardiff. Combined with our wider investment in St David’s, it will further strengthen the mix of retail, leisure and experiences we’re creating and give Gen Z in particular another reason to visit and spend time in the city centre.”

items.title: Poundland owners break silence and vow to protect 'as many jobs as possible'
items.summary: The discount retailer, whose thousands of staff have been left in the lurch as it waits to call in administrators, was bought by the US investment firm for less than £1 last November.
items.body:
Poundland owners break silence and vow to protect 'as many jobs as possible'
The owner of Poundland has broken its silence following criticism from the UK Government over its handling of the sale of the retailer.
Gordon Brothers has been slammed for rejecting a bid that would have saved the entire retailer, as opposed to carving up its 600 shops and risking thousands of jobs in the process.
The discount retailer, whose over 10,000- strong workforce has been left in the lurch as it waits to call in administrators, was bought by the closely guarded US investment firm for less than £1 last November.
A spokesman at Gordon Brothers today insisted it was looking at ‘all avenues’ in order to protect ‘as many jobs as possible.’
In the first remarks on the looming collapse, they said the business ‘has faced several years of instability.’
Government outrage: Ministers have demanded answers from US firm Gordon Brothers over Poundland, which has been on sale since September
They added: 'When Gordon Brothers acquired the business, it was in distress and required a radical restructure, urgent operational change and significant funding, which we provided to support the company’s ability to trade.
'In spite of our efforts and the tremendous efforts of management to deliver a turnaround, the business remains challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading.’
Hitting back at claims the company is just looking to profit, he said: ‘Our intent throughout the comprehensive sale process has been to protect as many jobs as possible and preserve value in order to deliver the best available outcome for the people, creditors and local communities who care about this business as much as we do.'
The statement said: ‘We are pursuing all avenues through the sale process to find a solution which protects as many jobs as possible and preserves value.
‘Work continues at pace, engaging in active discussions on offers with interested parties.’
It comes after Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds met the Gordon Brothers yesterday amid Government criticism of their handling of the retailer this week.
A source close to the business secretary said: ‘The Business Secretary has been firm that Gordon Brothers must do everything in their power to protect jobs and provide certainty for workers.
'He is pleased to have secured this commitment from Gordon Brothers in the meeting and will continue to hold the company to account and closely monitor developments.’
It is not yet clear yet whether Gordon Brothers will attend a grilling session by MPs on the business select committee next week.
It follows Andy Burnham’s remarks that he was ‘prepared to find what we can do’ to help save the chain.
Poundland's failure would mark one of the biggest High Street collapses since Debenhams closed its doors in 2021 with the loss of 12,000 jobs. It is currently lining up administrators before a deadline next week.
A Poundland distribution centre employing 270 staff in Makerfield – in Burnham’s constituency in Greater Manchester – is also at risk.
The Prime Minister told Poundland owners: ‘Come up with a practical solution that saves jobs and saves those stores because many of them are viable propositions.’
Business minister Kate Dearden also held talks with Poundland’s chief executive and chief finance officer, who are urging Gordon Brothers to agree to sell the whole company in one go.
There are two bidders who are interested in buying the whole company, the little-known Martin Property Group and Xyra Group.
Tesco has held talks over proposals to buy up to 150 Poundland stores while Poundstretcher owner Fortress also showed its interest in purchasing as many as 250 shops.
Bally Auluk, national officer for the shopworkers' union Usdaw, said: ‘We again call on the owners to hear the voice of our members by meeting directly with us. It is the least our members deserve, who have played a significant part in turning the company around and back to being profitable.’

items.title: Range Rover Evoque and Velar to be axed next year as new £90k electric GT becomes luxury brand's entry
items.summary: Jaguar Land Rover has confirmed that the Evoque (pictured) and Velar will cease production in the middle of next year, paving the way for the Range Rover brand to move further upmarket.
items.body:
Range Rover Evoque and Velar to be axed next year as new £90k electric GT becomes luxury brand's entry
Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has confirmed that the Evoque and Velar will cease production in the middle of next year, paving the way for the Range Rover brand to move further upmarket and appeal to a wealthier clientele.
Its two most affordable models will be replaced by the all-new Range Rover GT, the company's most car-like vehicle yet, which looks more like a jacked-up family saloon than an out-and-out SUV.
It marks the first time in the carmaker's near-60-year history that it will sell a vehicle that isn't a high-riding 4x4.
The new electric GT is expected to start from around £90,000, double the price of a new Evoque, which starts from £44,855.
The axeing of the two models will allow the Land Rover Discovery and a smaller, cheaper Defender to be repositioned as the entry points into JLR ownership, bosses claim.
But the demise of two of its most recognisable and widely copied vehicles also raises a further question: what luxury automotive products will Chinese brands replicate when designing their next generation of affordable SUVs with premium British styling?
Range Rover is ditching its cheapest model, the Evoque, next year. The new electric GT will become the entry point for Range Rover models at double the start price of around £90k
In a statement issued to This is Money, a JLR spokesman said: 'Both Range Rover Velar and Range Rover Evoque will continue to be sold in selected global markets where demand remains strong, throughout 2027.
'Production of both models will end in mid-2027 in line with their natural product lifecycles, as JLR's manufacturing facilities transition to build its next generation of vehicles.
'Solihull will continue to focus on producing Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and the forthcoming Jaguar Type 01, while Halewood will transition to produce the new Range Rover GT and a new model from the Defender family.'
With the GT offering a sleeker look and more svelte proportions, it appears the natural successor to the Velar.
However, with the outgoing SUV priced from £56,740, its replacement represents a near-60 per cent jump in price.
The Velar joined the Range Rover line-up as a more stylish alternative to the Range Rover Sport. While its coupe looks were widely liked, it was never among JLR's best sellers
With the new electric GT coming as the replacement and offering a sleek look and svelte proportions, it appears the natural successor to the outgoing Velar
While the Velar has been comprehensively outsold by the larger Range Rover and Range Rover Sport since it entered showrooms in 2017, the Evoque is a very different story.
When the first-generation model arrived in 2011, it became both a runaway success and JLR's most popular vehicle.
Its distinctive styling, compact city-friendly dimensions and badge appeal made it an instant hit with customers keen to join the Range Rover club without spending six-figure sums on one of its larger SUVs.
Famously, Victoria Beckham collaborated with Land Rover's design team, led by former design director Gerry McGovern, to create a limited-run Range Rover Evoque Special Edition, further boosting the vehicle's appeal and helping turn it into a commercial powerhouse.
When the first-generation Evoque arrived in 2011 as a three-door design, it became both a runaway success and JLR's most popular vehicle
The Evoque was initially a huge hit for JLR and regularly exceeded 100,000 annual sales in the mid 2010s
Famously, Victoria Beckham collaborated with Land Rover's design team, led by former design director Gerry McGovern, to create a limited-run Range Rover Evoque Special Edition
Before the Evoque arrived, JLR's annual global sales hovered around 144,000 vehicles.
In 2012, the first full year of Evoque availability, deliveries more than doubled to over 303,000 units, driven heavily by demand for the stylish compact SUV, which at launch was even offered as a three-door model.
At its peak, the Evoque accounted for one in every three JLR vehicles sold globally, with demand so strong that the Halewood factory switched to a 24-hour production schedule to keep up.
In 2016, JLR, owned by Indian giant Tata, described the Evoque as 'Land Rover's greatest sales success story' after amassing more than half a million sales across 180 countries in just five years.
By the time the second-generation model arrived in 2018, however, the premium compact SUV market had become far more crowded, making it harder for the Evoque to stand out. It also suffered a series of reliability issues that dented its reputation.
The Jaecoo 7 has earned the nickname the 'Temu Range Rover' for its likeness to the Velar but at half the price. The family-friendly Chinese SUV is the second best-selling new car in 2026
In 2019, JLR won a 'significant' legal case in the Chinese courts against a Landwind's X7 SUV (left), which was deemed a copycat of the Evoque (right)
The Beijing Chaoyang District Court ruled that the Range Rover Evoque (right) had five unique features copied by the Chinese model (left)
What will Chinese brands copy now?
Despite not being among JLR's best sellers, the Velar and Evoque remain two of the most frequently replicated vehicle designs on the market, particularly among Chinese newcomers.
The Jaecoo 7, Britain's second best-selling new car of 2026 and the model that topped the UK sales charts over the past two months, has been nicknamed the 'Temu Range Rover' because of its close resemblance to the larger of the two Range Rover models being discontinued.
In 2019, JLR won a 'significant' legal case in China against a company that produced a copy of the Evoque.
The British carmaker said the Beijing Chaoyang District Court ruled that the Range Rover Evoque had five unique design features copied in a model called the Landwind X7, built by Jiangling Motor Corporation.
As a result of the verdict, all sales, manufacturing and marketing of the Landwind vehicle were ordered to cease immediately, with JLR also receiving financial compensation. The company was awarded RMB1.5million, approximately £170,000.
Range Rover's 'most car-like' model ever: The new electric Range Rover GT will be the new entry point to Range Rover ownership. At £90k, it's going to be double the price of the Evoque
The GT's svelte body is a bold deviation from Range Rover convention. In fact, it looks like a Range Rover Sport that's had a grand piano dropped onto it from a great height
Paving the way for Range Rover to be more expensive
The Evoque and Velar's departure from production lines will coincide with the arrival of the all-new, and significantly more expensive, GT model.
It will become the new and substantially higher entry point into Range Rover ownership as JLR looks to position its 'House of Brands' at distinct price levels.
A new Defender Sport is currently under development and will be unveiled next year, becoming the most affordable model in the Defender range alongside the Discovery, which currently starts from just under £70,000.
JLR has already confirmed it will kill off the smaller Discovery Sport, the Evoque's sister model, at the end of this year.
The GT will be the first all-electric Range Rover to use the company's Electrified Modular Architecture (EMA), a highly adaptable platform created primarily for its mid-sized premium vehicles.
This differs from the Modular Longitudinal Architecture (MLA) underpinning the forthcoming Range Rover Electric and Range Rover Sport Electric.
However, both have been designed to accommodate a variety of powertrains, including battery-electric, plug-in hybrid, self-charging hybrid, petrol and diesel. There is still no word on when a combustion-engined GT will be offered.
The GT will also differ from the Jaguar Electrified Architecture (JEA), which underpins the controversial new £120,000 Type 01 electric grand tourer.
However, just like its Jaguar sibling, the Range Rover GT will be sold as standard with a luxurious four-seat layout.
Bosses say that despite its reduced ground clearance, the GT will be able to tackle tough off-road terrains like any other Range Rover
Unlike the Jag, the Range Rover GT does have a glass rear window and conventional rear-view mirror. Though it will have four seats as standard, like its Jaguar brethren
That said, bosses insist the GT will retain the off-road capability expected of a Range Rover.
Martin Limpert, managing director of Range Rover, said it will be the 'most car-like' Range Rover ever.
'The Range Rover GT will redefine the grand-touring segment with the ability to deliver beautiful and engaging GT poise, proportions and long-distance refinement while offering capabilities no conventional GT can match,' he said.
'We have spent the last few years working obsessively on the fundamentals of the GT formula, reinterpreted in a sophisticated, uniquely Range Rover way.
'The result is the most car-like, yet unmistakably capable, Range Rover ever created, now possible on our electrified EMA architecture - complementing our existing powertrain portfolio to deliver a complete set of options for every customer need.
'Its blend of effortless EV performance, first-class long-haul refinement and all-terrain capability is pure Range Rover, while its calming interior previews our vision of a modern grand tourer.'

items.body:
Asda expands ready meal range with 87 products
Asda has expanded its own-label ready meal range with 87 new additions as it focuses on innovation within the category for shoppers.
The retailer aims to meet the demand for variety in everyday meals and offer convenient options that fit consumers’ busy lifestyles.
The business is expanding its Indian-inspired range, Born Bahia, with the addition of two meal deal boxes for two people priced at £6 per portion.
There is the Tandoori Smoked Butter Chicken and Slow Cooked Beef Madras and Kashmiri Style Korma Chicken and Tikka Masala added to the line.
Additionally, there are also two new premium pasta dishes designed for customers who want to experience restaurant-style dining at home.
Asda’s Exceptional range now includes Lobster & Prawn Ravioli with Brown Butter and Beef & Chianti Tortelloni with Parmesan Butter for £4 each.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
The supermarket retailer is also bringing innovation to classic dishes, with the launch of a Pizzagne, a mix of lasagne and pizzas in two varieties for £6.57 each.
There are also Chinese-inspired dishes with a Salt & Pepper Chicken Munch Box, which costs £8.24. The munch box features salt and pepper chicken, egg fried rice, vegetable spring rolls, and prawn crackers.
Rachel Ambler, product development manager of ready meals at Asda said: “This new range of ready meals all falls back on our commitment to give customers more of what they love whilst making sure they’re still at Asda prices.
“We’ve really looked to add more novelty and creativity to our ranges to add that touch of excitement to family weekly meals, whilst also ensuring our Exceptional range provides restaurant-worthy quality and taste, but without the premium price tag attached.”

items.title: What vape retailers need to know to avoid £2,500 fines | Viewpoint: Dr Marina Murphy
items.summary: Vape retailers in the UK have been experiencing significant regulatory changes, with last year's ban on disposable vapes, the introduction of Vaping Products Duty, and potentially major changes to display and packaging regulations all impacting business. In addition to this, retailers now also have to… This story continues at What vape retailers need to know to avoid £2,500 fines | Viewpoint: Dr Marina Murphy Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
In addition to this, retailers now also have to navigate another complex set of rules as new laws came into effect on 29 October under the Tobacco and Vapes Act.
Here are four things retailers need to know:
- Introduction of a minimum age of sale of 18 for all consumer nicotine products and zero-nicotine vapes
On 29th October, it becomes illegal to sell any vaping product or consumer nicotine product, including nicotine pouches and zero-nicotine vapes, to anyone under the age of 18. Retailers need to make sure all staff are trained on the new age of sale and enforce strict ID checks. This applies to both online and in-store retail, so if you operate a retail website, you must ensure that you have an age verification system in place. If a retailer commits an offence of selling nicotine products to an underage person, they can receive a Fixed Penalty Notice (FPN) of £200 in England, Wales and Scotland, or a £250 FPN in Northern Ireland.
- Ban on vending machines containing vapes or non-medicinal nicotine products
All vending machines selling vapes, zero-nicotine vapes, or other consumer nicotine products will be completely banned. If you have any vending machines containing tobacco or nicotine products, remove them before 29th October. Retailers can face a summary conviction fine of up to £2,500 (or up to £5,000 in Northern Ireland) if prosecuted in court, or a FPN of £200 (in England, Scotland, and Wales) or £250 (in Northern Ireland) issued by local authorities. Importantly, the person who manages or controls the premises where the vending is located is responsible for complying with the vending machine ban, not the vending machine owner. Retailers who want to have a vending machine removed should contact the owner as soon as possible.
- Ban on the free distribution of vapes and other consumer nicotine products
Handing out free samples or free distribution of vapes and consumer nicotine products will also be prohibited from 29th October. As part of this, it will also be illegal to give a coupon or sell a coupon at a substantial discount for a vaping or nicotine product where the purpose or effect is to promote the product. This not only covers the distribution of free samples, it also means that deals such as buy one, get one free, will no longer be legal.
- Proxy purchasing for nicotine pouches
It will be an offence for anyone aged 18 or over to buy, or attempt to buy, vaping and nicotine products on behalf of someone under 18. While it is already illegal to buy cigarettes or vapes on behalf of someone underage, this will be extended to all nicotine products from 29th October. All retail staff should be alert to prevent proxy purchasing. Staff should be trained to identify situations where a customer may be attempting to buy these products for someone underage. If staff suspect proxy purchasing, they should refuse the sale.
Dr Marina Murphy is head of external affairs UK and scientific affairs at Haypp

items.title: Allwyn UK aims to improve National Lottery experience with leadership changes
items.summary: Allwyn UK has announced a new leadership structure to deliver the next stage of its transformation of The National Lottery. The new senior team structure is designed to accelerate growth, increase returns for Good Causes and improve the experience for players and retail partners by… This story continues at Allwyn UK aims to improve National Lottery experience with leadership changes Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The new senior team structure is designed to accelerate growth, increase returns for Good Causes and improve the experience for players and retail partners by bringing key commercial, customer and technology capabilities closer together around Allwyn’s retail and digital channels, while elevating the role of marketing across the business.
To strengthen the connection between supporting Good Causes and playing The National Lottery, a new dedicated director of social impact role will focus on communicating the positive impact of The National Lottery on communities across the UK, creating even more compelling reasons for people to play.
Current chief impact officer Alastair Ruxton will take on this role, reporting to the CEO, to focus on the connection between Good Causes, social value and The National Lottery’s wider proposition.
As part of the focus on improving technology and customer experience, the chief technology officer and managing director, digital roles will end as technology capabilities will become more directly integrated into digital, retail and security.
Responsibility for strategy and the future direction of the business will move to the CEO, and as a result, the chief strategy & transformation officer role will also end.
Current chief technology officer Mark Smith will leave the business, but continue as technology strategy adviser until June 2027, providing continuity as the new structure is established.
Richard Dawkins, managing director, digital, will leave the business in December 2026 after nearly three years, having led its digital business through a significant period of change and driven innovation in the games portfolio.
Sarah Venning, chief strategy & transformation officer, will leave Allwyn at the end of November 2026, having played an important role in shaping the company’s strategy and helping lead its transformation.
Two further new roles will be created to support this next phase of growth. A new chief digital officer (CDO) role will bring together responsibility for digital products and channels, customer experience, technology, data and platforms, automation and AI, alongside accountability for the commercial performance of Allwyn’s digital channels.
A new chief marketing officer (CMO) role will bring together brand, marketing, creative, CRM, communications, product marketing, winners’ services and customer experience to create a stronger and more consistent connection with players.
Stephen Taylor will join as interim chief marketing officer on 17 November 2026. He brings more than 30 years’ marketing experience across major consumer brands including PayPal, Samsung, Nokia and Pizza Express. Taylor joins from CMO Thrive, the strategic marketing advisory business he founded.
The new structure will take effect from 1 December 2026.
Chief executive Phil Walker said: “The transformation of The National Lottery has involved an enormous amount of work across our business. Our challenge now is to turn that transformation into stronger growth, a better experience for players and retail partners, and more money for Good Causes.
“That means putting customers closer to our decisions, giving our Retail and Digital businesses the capabilities they need to compete and innovate, and creating much clearer accountability for performance.
“Good Causes are at the heart of what makes The National Lottery special. We have a real opportunity to help more people understand the extraordinary difference players make through The National Lottery and make that an even stronger reason to play.
“Changes of this scale inevitably affect people who have played important roles in getting us to where we are today. This next stage builds on what they have helped us achieve, and I want to thank them personally for the contribution they and their teams have made to The National Lottery.”
